name: 211 Ontario (meals and food help)
description: A free 24/7 helpline funded by the Ontario government and United Ways that connects callers to food help near them, from Meals on Wheels programs to community dining, grocery help and food banks. Community Navigators answer in over 150 languages; dial 211, or toll free 1-877-330-3213.
intakeNote: Dial 211 (or toll free 1-877-330-3213) any time, 24/7; a real person answers and connects you to services near you.

name: 211 Ontario (rides and transportation help)
description: A free 24/7 helpline funded by the Ontario government and United Ways that connects callers to local community services, including seniors' rides, accessible transit and volunteer driver programs near them. Community Navigators answer in over 150 languages; dial 211, or toll free 1-877-330-3213.
intakeNote: Dial 211 (or toll free 1-877-330-3213) any time, 24/7; a real person answers and connects you to services near you.

name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
description: Canada's suicide crisis helpline, funded by the Government of Canada and led by the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health. Call or text 9-8-8 free of charge, any hour of any day, in English or French, whether you are struggling yourself or worried about someone you love.
intakeNote: Call or text 9-8-8 at any hour; free, confidential, and no referral needed.

name: Advocacy Centre for the Elderly (ACE)
description: A specialty community legal clinic funded through Legal Aid Ontario that serves low-income seniors, the first of its kind in Canada. Its lawyers give free advice and representation on elder abuse, health care consent, powers of attorney, home care, retirement home and long-term care problems. Direct casework focuses on the Greater Toronto Area; callers elsewhere in Ontario get information and referrals.
intakeNote: Call the intake line on Monday, Wednesday or Friday, 9 a.m. to noon or 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.; intake is by phone only.

name: Coverage for Seniors (Alberta Blue Cross)
description: A Government of Alberta benefit, administered by Alberta Blue Cross, that gives every senior 65 and over premium-free coverage for prescription drugs, diabetes supplies, ambulance trips and some other health services. It is added to your Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan automatically the month after you turn 65.
intakeNote: No application needed; coverage starts automatically once your age is validated with AHCIP. Claims questions go to Alberta Blue Cross at 1-800-661-6995.

name: Health Link 811 (Alberta)
description: Alberta's free 24-hour health advice line, run by Primary Care Alberta, a provincial health agency, in partnership with Alberta Health Services. Dial 811 to reach a registered nurse any time; the line can also connect you with dietitians, dementia specialists, and mental health and rehabilitation clinicians.
intakeNote: Dial 811 from anywhere in Alberta, any time; online nurse chat and callback requests are available at primarycarealberta.ca.

name: Dental and Optical Assistance for Seniors
description: A Government of Alberta program that pays up to $5,000 every 5 years for basic dental care and up to $230 every 3 years toward prescription eyeglasses for lower-income seniors 65 and over. Your eligibility is assessed automatically once you apply for Seniors Financial Assistance.
intakeNote: Apply through the Seniors Financial Assistance application at sfa.alberta.ca; claims are handled by Alberta Blue Cross at 1-800-661-6995.

name: Seniors Home Adaptation and Repair Program (SHARP)
description: A Government of Alberta loan program that lends seniors up to $40,000 at low interest for home repairs, adaptations and renovations such as stair lifts, bathroom upgrades or a new furnace. The loan is secured against the home and repaid when it is sold.
intakeNote: Complete the Loan Application and Agreement form with your property tax assessment and cost estimates or receipts, then submit online, by fax or by mail.

name: Alberta Supports Contact Centre
description: The Government of Alberta's front door to more than 30 programs and 120 services, including all of the seniors financial assistance programs. One call connects seniors and family caregivers to benefits and local offices, and staff can also explain the automatic 25 percent seniors discount on registry services such as driver's licence renewals.
intakeNote: Call 1-877-644-9992 (780-644-9992 in Edmonton), Monday to Friday 7:30 am to 8 pm, or visit a local Alberta Supports office.

name: Seniors Property Tax Deferral Program
description: A Government of Alberta program that pays your residential property taxes for you through a low-interest home equity loan, repaid when the home is sold. Homeowners 65 and over with at least 25 percent equity in their home can apply.
intakeNote: Apply with the loan application form and submit online at seniors.alberta.ca/submit-documents, by fax or by mail; call 1-877-644-9992 for help.

name: Alberta Seniors Benefit
description: A monthly Government of Alberta benefit that tops up income for seniors 65 and over with lower incomes. One Seniors Financial Assistance application, which you can file up to a year before your 65th birthday, also connects you to Alberta's other seniors benefits.
intakeNote: Apply online at sfa.alberta.ca, by printed form, or call 1-877-644-9992 to have one mailed.

name: Special Needs Assistance for Seniors
description: A Government of Alberta benefit that gives low-income seniors a lump sum, up to $5,872 in a benefit year, toward items like appliances, a bed, some medical equipment and prescription co-payments. You send in receipts or estimates and the province pays its share.
intakeNote: Apply for Seniors Financial Assistance first, then submit receipts or estimates through your MyAlberta Seniors account, by upload, fax or mail.

name: Supplementary Accommodation Benefit
description: A Government of Alberta benefit that helps low-income seniors pay the monthly accommodation charge in a continuing care home, while leaving at least $373 a month for personal costs. It arrives combined with the Alberta Seniors Benefit in one monthly payment.
intakeNote: Covered by the same Seniors Financial Assistance application at sfa.alberta.ca; call 1-877-644-9992 with questions.

name: Family Violence Info Line (elder abuse help)
description: A 24-hour Government of Alberta line for anyone worried about elder abuse or family violence. Call or text 310-1818 for information, advice and referrals in more than 170 languages.
intakeNote: Call or text 310-1818 any time, day or night; no area code needed inside Alberta.

name: Protection for Persons in Care reporting line
description: A Government of Alberta reporting line for abuse of adults who receive publicly funded care or support services, including seniors in continuing care homes. Anyone can call to report a concern and the province follows up under the Protection for Persons in Care Act.
intakeNote: Call 1-888-357-9339 to make a report; anyone who witnesses or suspects abuse of an adult in care can call.

name: Alzheimer Society Durham First Link
description: First Link connects people living with dementia and their care partners to one on one support, education, and support groups, plus referral to the MINT Memory Clinic for memory assessment. This is a registered charity offering community based dementia support across Durham Region.
intakeNote: Call the toll-free line, email intake@alzheimerdurham.com, or fill out the online First Link referral form on the contact page, and a First Link Coordinator will follow up; the MINT Memory Clinic needs a referral from a primary care provider.

name: Alzheimer Society Peel Adult Day Programs
description: A non-profit community service run by Alzheimer Society Peel at three Mississauga locations (Sam McCallion Day Centre, Evelyn's Place, and Brunel Day Centre), offering supervised social and recreational activities, meals, music therapy, and dementia-trained staff for people living with dementia. Daily fees range from $21 for a standard day to $28 for the longest extended-hours option.
intakeNote: Call 905-278-3667 ext. 307 or email direct.support@alzheimerpeel.com to reach the dementia support team; no diagnosis or doctor's referral is needed, and a doctor or agency can also refer a family using the online First Link form.

name: Alzheimer Society Peel Dementia Resource Consultants
description: A free program run by Alzheimer Society Peel, a registered charity, offering one on one information, care strategies, and emotional support for people living with dementia and their care partners across Peel Region. No diagnosis or referral is needed to connect with a Dementia Resource Consultant, and the related First Link program also takes doctor and agency referrals.
intakeNote: Call 905-278-3667 ext. 307 or email direct.support@alzheimerpeel.com to reach the dementia support team; no diagnosis or doctor's referral is needed, and a doctor or agency can also refer a family using the online First Link form.

name: Alzheimer Society of Toronto
description: A registered charity offering free support groups, one on one counselling, and education sessions for people with dementia and their care partners in Toronto. Support groups include options for young onset dementia, frontotemporal dementia, and Lewy body dementia, and the Society also runs the Active Minds Club day program for people diagnosed before age 65.
intakeNote: Call 416-322-6560, email info@alz.to, or fill out the online Get Started form, and an Intake Coordinator will follow up to plan next steps (a doctor can also send a referral).

name: Alzheimer Society York Region Minds in Motion
description: A non-profit community program from the Alzheimer Society of York Region. A person with early or mid-stage dementia and their care partner attend eight weekly sessions together that mix gentle physical activity with social and cognitive stimulation.
intakeNote: Families call 905-726-3477 (toll-free 1-888-414-5550) or reach the general inbox at info@alzheimer-york.com. Some programs, like the D.A.Y. Centre and First Link, also take direct referrals from doctors, hospitals, and family members.

name: Alzheimer Society York Region D.A.Y. Centre
description: A registered charity's adult day program for people diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease or another dementia, running since 1985. Staff lead structured social and recreational activities at centres in Aurora, Thornhill, and Stouffville, giving caregivers a break during the day.
intakeNote: Families call 905-726-3477 (toll-free 1-888-414-5550) or reach the general inbox at info@alzheimer-york.com. Some programs, like the D.A.Y. Centre and First Link, also take direct referrals from doctors, hospitals, and family members.

name: Fair PharmaCare
description: Income-based drug coverage from the Government of British Columbia that helps families pay for prescription drugs, dispensing fees and some medical supplies. You register once and are covered for life, and the less your household earns the more the plan pays.
intakeNote: Register once online at my.gov.bc.ca/ahdc or call 1-800-663-7100; you must be enrolled in MSP.

name: HealthLink BC 811
description: The Government of British Columbia's free health information line. Dial 811 any time, day or night, to speak with a registered nurse, and reach dietitians, exercise professionals or an overnight pharmacist at set hours, with translation in more than 130 languages.
intakeNote: Just dial 811 from anywhere in BC; nurses answer 24/7.

name: Better at Home
description: Non-medical home support funded by the Government of BC and managed by United Way British Columbia. Local community agencies offer light housekeeping, grocery shopping, rides to appointments, friendly visits, yard work and snow shovelling so seniors can keep living at home.
intakeNote: Find your local Better at Home program with the map at betterathome.ca and contact it directly; the provincial office is 604-268-1312.

name: BC Rebate for Accessible Home Adaptations (BC RAHA)
description: A BC Housing program, formerly called HAFI, that gives lower-income homeowners and renters rebates for accessibility adaptations such as grab bars, ramps, stair rails and walk-in showers. Applications are taken first come, first served, and funding renews every April 1.
intakeNote: Download the homeowner or tenant application from BC Housing or call 1-800-257-7756; submit through the program upload form.

name: BC Home Renovation Tax Credit for Seniors
description: A Government of British Columbia refundable tax credit of up to $1,000 a year for people 65 and over, and for persons with disabilities, who renovate their home to make it safer or easier to get around. It returns 10 percent of eligible renovation costs, up to $10,000 in expenses a year.
intakeNote: Claim it on your income tax return using Schedule BC(S12); call 1-877-387-3332 with questions.

name: BC Home Owner Grant (higher amount for 65+)
description: A Government of British Columbia grant that lowers the annual property tax bill on your principal home, with a higher grant amount for owners aged 65 and over. You apply again each year after your tax notice arrives.
intakeNote: Apply each year online or by phone at 1-888-355-2700 once you get your property tax notice.

name: SAFER (Shelter Aid for Elderly Renters)
description: A BC Housing program that pays monthly cash toward rent for British Columbians aged 60 and over whose rent takes more than 30 percent of their income. The province funds it so lower-income seniors can stay in their own rental homes.
intakeNote: Download the application from BC Housing or call 1-800-257-7756; submit by online upload, mail, fax or in person.

name: Office of the Seniors Advocate BC information line
description: An independent office of the BC provincial government that watches over seniors services and runs a toll-free information line. Senior service specialists help seniors and family caregivers find the right programs and work through problems with health care, housing, income and transportation.
intakeNote: Call 1-877-952-3181, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

name: BC Seniors Supplement
description: An automatic monthly top-up from the Government of British Columbia for low-income seniors who receive Old Age Security and the Guaranteed Income Supplement. There is no application; payments start on their own about a month after your federal benefits begin.
intakeNote: No application needed; payment is automatic for eligible seniors. Call 1-866-866-0800 with questions.

name: BC Property Tax Deferment Program (55+)
description: A Government of British Columbia loan program that lets homeowners aged 55 and over put off paying their annual property taxes until the home is sold or transferred. The province pays the tax bill for you and charges low interest on the balance.
intakeNote: Apply and renew online through eTaxBC; call 1-888-355-2700 for help.

name: BC Palliative Care Benefits (Plan P)
description: A Government of British Columbia PharmaCare plan for people who choose to receive end-of-life care at home. It covers 100 percent of palliative medications on the Plan P list, and medical supplies and equipment come through your health authority.
intakeNote: Your doctor or nurse practitioner registers you; coverage is usually in place within a day. PharmaCare questions: 1-800-663-7100.

name: BC Bus Pass Program
description: A Government of British Columbia program that sells a subsidized annual transit pass to low-income seniors, including those receiving the Guaranteed Income Supplement or its Allowances. The pass costs $45 for the year and works on BC Transit and TransLink services.
intakeNote: Apply online at myselfserve.gov.bc.ca/BusPass or call 1-866-866-0800, Monday to Friday 9 am to 4 pm.

name: handyDART (Kelowna Regional Transit)
description: A BC Transit service that gives door-to-door, shared rides in the Kelowna area for people with a permanent or temporary disability that keeps them from using regular buses on their own. Drivers help riders board and exit, picking up and dropping off at an accessible door.
intakeNote: Register first with the free handyDART application form, then book trips through the handyDART office at 250-762-3278.

name: Taxi Saver (Kelowna)
description: A BC Transit program that sells half-price taxi voucher books to registered handyDART riders in Kelowna, covering 50 percent of the taxi fare for one-time trips when handyDART is not available. Riders call a participating local taxi company and pay with the vouchers.
intakeNote: Enroll through handyDART registration (include a passport photo with the application); the Kelowna handyDART office at 250-762-3278 handles registration.

name: handyDART (Victoria Regional Transit)
description: A BC Transit service that gives door-to-door, shared rides around the Victoria region for people whose disability keeps them from using regular buses. Fares are the same as regular Victoria buses, including a senior rate on monthly passes.
intakeNote: Complete the handyDART application form first (a medical verification form from a health professional can support it); once registered, book trips up to 14 days ahead at 250-727-7811, press 0, or online. To cancel, call 250-479-0004.

name: Taxi Saver (Victoria)
description: A BC Transit program that sells half-price taxi voucher books to registered handyDART riders in the Victoria region, covering 50 percent of the taxi fare for trips handyDART cannot serve. Riders book with a participating taxi company and pay with the vouchers.
intakeNote: Mail your handyPASS number, return address and a $40 cheque payable to BC Transit to the Taxi Saver Program, 520 Gorge Road East, PO Box 9861, Victoria, BC V8W 9T5; call the Taxi Saver Office at 250-995-5618 with questions.

name: Bereavement Authority of Ontario
description: The government delegated authority that licenses Ontario's funeral homes, cemeteries and crematoriums under provincial law. Families can check that a provider is licensed, read plain language guides on funeral costs and their rights, and file a complaint if something goes wrong (toll free 1-844-493-6356).
intakeNote: Call 647-483-2645 (toll free 1-844-493-6356) or use the public register and complaint forms at thebao.ca.

name: Brampton Meals on Wheels
description: A registered charity that delivers hot and frozen meals to seniors and other adults in Brampton who cannot cook for themselves. Volunteers bring hot meals Monday to Friday between 11:30 a.m. and 1 p.m., and frozen meals every Friday morning, with diabetic, low sodium, pureed, minced and other diet options available.
intakeNote: Call the office Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 3 p.m., or use the contact form on the website to place a new order or ask questions.

name: Calgary Public Library Homebound Readers
description: A free service from Calgary Public Library, the city's public library system, where trained volunteers choose, deliver and exchange library materials for people who cannot get to a branch because of health or mobility issues. Deliveries often come with a friendly visit, and through Libraries in Residence the library also rotates collections through care centres, lodges and seniors residences across Calgary.
intakeNote: Call 403-260-2702 to sign up for Homebound Readers; a care home's wellness or recreation coordinator can call the same number to arrange Libraries in Residence.

name: Calgary Transit Access
description: Calgary Transit's shared ride, door-to-door bus service, a City of Calgary service for people whose disability keeps them from using regular buses and CTrains. Once registered, riders book trips by phone or online. Seniors 65 and over can also buy a reduced-price annual seniors pass for regular transit, with a lower-price low-income seniors option for those who qualify by income.
intakeNote: Call 403-537-7770 to check eligibility and request an application; a medical professional completes one section, then an in-person interview is scheduled within about 5 to 10 business days. Registered riders book trips at 403-537-7777.

name: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre
description: The Government of Canada's central fraud reporting service, jointly managed by the RCMP, the Ontario Provincial Police and the Competition Bureau. Seniors and families can call to report a scam, check whether a call or offer is genuine, and learn what to do after money or personal information has been taken.
intakeNote: Call 1-888-495-8501, Monday to Friday 10 am to 4:45 pm Eastern time, or report a scam online any time through the reporting system at reportcyberandfraud.canada.ca.

name: Canadian Dental Care Plan
description: A Government of Canada benefit, administered by Sun Life, that pays much of the cost of dental care for people without private dental insurance, including cleanings, fillings, x-rays and dentures. Seniors of any age qualify if the household income is under $90,000, last year's taxes are filed, and they live in Canada. Applications for the 2026-2027 benefit year are open.
intakeNote: Apply online through My Service Canada Account or Canada.ca, or call Service Canada at 1-833-537-4342 (TTY 1-833-677-6262); a trusted helper can apply with the senior on the line to give consent.

name: Canadian Hearing Services Hearing Clinics
description: A registered charity running 10 hearing clinics across Ontario, including Toronto, Mississauga, and Newmarket in York Region, offering hearing tests, hearing aid consultations, and fittings with a 90 day trial. This is a non-profit community service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call 1-866-518-0000, email audiology@chs.ca, or book online (Ontario residents only) for a hearing test or hearing aid consultation. No referral is needed.

name: Canadian Red Cross Friendly Calls Program
description: Trained Red Cross volunteers call people age 18 and up on a regular basis just to check in, talk, and share wellbeing resources, an easy way to feel less alone. It is free and available by phone anywhere in Canada, including every city in the GTA. The Canadian Red Cross is a federally chartered registered charity, and this is a public community support service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: There is no single phone number across these programs. Families call the specific line: Toronto Transportation and Meals on Wheels at 416-236-3180, Burlington Transportation at 1-844-843-7331 ext 2, Burlington Meals on Wheels at 905-637-5664, or the national Friendly Calls Program at 1-833-979-9779.

name: Canadian Red Cross Meals on Wheels
description: The Canadian Red Cross delivers hot, nutritious meals to people who cannot cook for themselves, with a volunteer who checks in at the door. Today this is confirmed only in Etobicoke (part of Toronto) and in the City of Burlington plus Flamborough. The Canadian Red Cross is a federally chartered registered charity, and this is a public community support service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: There is no single phone number across these programs. Families call the specific line: Toronto Transportation and Meals on Wheels at 416-236-3180, Burlington Transportation at 1-844-843-7331 ext 2, Burlington Meals on Wheels at 905-637-5664, or the national Friendly Calls Program at 1-833-979-9779.

name: Canadian Red Cross Transportation
description: The Canadian Red Cross drives seniors and adults with disabilities who cannot use public transit to medical appointments, shopping, and social outings, using cars, mid-sized vans, and accessible vehicles. Today this covers all of Toronto through the Toronto Ride coalition and the City of Burlington only. The Canadian Red Cross is a federally chartered registered charity, and this is a public community support service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: There is no single phone number across these programs. Families call the specific line: Toronto Transportation and Meals on Wheels at 416-236-3180, Burlington Transportation at 1-844-843-7331 ext 2, Burlington Meals on Wheels at 905-637-5664, or the national Friendly Calls Program at 1-833-979-9779.

name: Access-A-Bus (Transit Cape Breton, formerly Handi-Trans)
description: Access-A-Bus, long known locally as Handi-Trans, is the Cape Breton Regional Municipality's door-to-door bus service run by Transit Cape Breton for riders whose disabilities keep them off the regular buses. It serves all communities in the CBRM and is meant for social outings, shopping, and recreation as well as medical appointments. Register once by phone, then book rides on the same line.
intakeNote: Call the Access-A-Bus line at 902-539-4336, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., to register and then to book rides.

name: Low-Income Property Tax Exemption (CBRM)
description: The Cape Breton Regional Municipality takes up to $300 a year off the property tax bill for lower-income homeowners, including many seniors on fixed incomes. If the home is your primary residence and your household income is under $40,800, you can apply with a short sworn form each tax year. Call 311 to have the form mailed or emailed to you.
intakeNote: Pick up or request the application form by calling 311, complete and swear it, and return it to the Citizen Service Centre at City Hall, 320 Esplanade, Sydney, before the yearly deadline.

name: CHATS In-Home Services (Home Help)
description: CHATS sends trained Home Support Workers and Personal Support Workers into a senior's own home for up to eight hours a month of help with light housekeeping, meal preparation, and personal care like bathing and dressing, with in-home relief for family caregivers. CHATS is a registered charity, so this is a non-profit community service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call 905-713-6596 or toll-free 1-877-452-4287, or email seniorshelp@chats.on.ca; CHATS follows up for an initial visit and intake assessment before building an individualized care plan.

name: CHATS Home Adaptation & Maintenance Program
description: This CHATS program installs grab bars, handrails, and other minor safety renovations after a free in-home safety assessment, and offers seasonal yard care, eavestrough cleaning, window cleaning, and snow clearing. It has helped over 2,100 clients since 2009. CHATS is a registered charity, so this is a non-profit community service, not a private contractor.
intakeNote: Call 905-713-6596 or toll-free 1-877-452-4287, or email seniorshelp@chats.on.ca; CHATS follows up for an initial visit and intake assessment before building an individualized care plan.

name: CHATS Meals on Wheels
description: CHATS delivers more than 100 frozen entrees, soups, and desserts to seniors' homes on a weekly, order-as-needed basis, including diabetic, low fat, low salt, vegetarian, pureed, minced, and halal options, plus a friendly volunteer check-in with each delivery. CHATS is a registered charity, so this is a non-profit community service.
intakeNote: Call 905-713-6596 or toll-free 1-877-452-4287, or email seniorshelp@chats.on.ca; CHATS follows up for an initial visit and intake assessment before building an individualized care plan.

name: CHATS Community Transportation (iRIDEplus)
description: CHATS' iRIDEplus program provides local and long-distance grouped drives to medical appointments, adult day programs, errands, and social outings for residents of York Region and South Simcoe, over 3500 drives a month. CHATS is a registered charity, so this is a non-profit community service, not a private ride company.
intakeNote: Call 905-713-6596 or toll-free 1-877-452-4287, or email seniorshelp@chats.on.ca; CHATS follows up for an initial visit and intake assessment before building an individualized care plan.

name: Circle of Care Adult Day Program
description: Circle of Care's Adult Day Program in Vaughan gives adults with memory loss or physical frailty a supervised place to spend the day, with meals, activities, and caregiver respite. It is a program of a registered charity that is a system partner of Sinai Health, a non-profit community service.
intakeNote: Call the main line at (416) 635-2860, or Ontario Health atHome at 1-833-515-1234 to be referred for government-funded home care.

name: Circle of Care Personal Support at Home
description: Personal Support Workers from Circle of Care help with bathing, dressing, meal prep, and light housekeeping in the client's own home, with relief for family caregivers. Circle of Care is a registered charity and a system partner of Sinai Health, so this is a non-profit community service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call the main line at (416) 635-2860, or Ontario Health atHome at 1-833-515-1234 to be referred for government-funded home care.

name: Circle of Care Meals on Wheels
description: Circle of Care's Meals on Wheels delivers nutritious frozen meals, including kosher options, to seniors and adults with disabilities across Toronto and into southern York Region. Circle of Care is a registered charity and a system partner of Sinai Health, so this is a non-profit community service.
intakeNote: Call the main line at (416) 635-2860, or Ontario Health atHome at 1-833-515-1234 to be referred for government-funded home care.

name: Circle of Care Bereavement Support
description: Circle of Care's Bereavement Support offers free grief counselling, support groups, and art therapy for adults across Ontario grieving the death of a close family member or friend, in person, by phone, or online. This free program is run by a registered charity that is a system partner of Sinai Health, a non-profit community service.
intakeNote: Call the main line at (416) 635-2860, or Ontario Health atHome at 1-833-515-1234 to be referred for government-funded home care.

name: Senior Fire Safety and Lock Box Program
description: A City of Brandon fire department program that mounts a small locked key box outside a senior's home so firefighters and paramedics can get in during an emergency without breaking the door. Brandon Fire and Emergency Services inspects and secures each box after it is installed, and pairs the program with fire safety education for older adults.
intakeNote: Buy the lock box through Seniors for Seniors at 204-571-2050, install it, then email fire@brandon.ca to book the fire department inspection.

name: Brandon Access Transit
description: Brandon Access Transit is a City of Brandon service that gives door-to-door rides within Brandon to people with disabilities who cannot use the regular bus, including a call-back service for medical appointments. Trips are booked by phone with the dispatch office. Fares match regular Brandon Transit, where seniors 60 and older already pay a reduced fare.
intakeNote: Complete the two application forms, both signed by your family doctor, and email them to accesstransit@brandon.ca or drop them at 723 Rosser Ave Unit A; book trips at 204-729-2437, Monday to Friday.

name: Burlington Seniors' Centre and 55+ Programs
description: The City of Burlington runs recreation and social programs for adults 55 and over, centred on the Burlington Seniors' Centre at 2285 New Street. Options include fitness and arts programs, music, pickleball, day trips, a free bike lending program, and the Bistro Lounge serving fresh, affordable lunches on weekdays.
intakeNote: Register through the Live and Play portal (cityofburlington.perfectmind.com) or call 905-335-7777; a new program booklet comes out each season.

name: Burlington Windrow Clearing Program
description: A City of Burlington service that clears the windrow, the pile of snow the plow leaves at the end of the driveway, within about 36 hours of a snowfall from December 1 to March 31. The seasonal fee is $150 plus HST, and seniors 65 and over and residents with disabilities or low incomes pay half price.
intakeNote: Register in the fall through your Live and Play account, at Service Burlington (426 Brant Street) or at the Burlington Seniors' Centre; 2026-27 registration details come out in September 2026.

name: Burlington Low-Income Property Tax Reduction
description: A City of Burlington program that takes $575 off the property tax bill for senior homeowners with low incomes. Seniors 65 and over receiving the Guaranteed Income Supplement qualify, as do homeowners receiving ODSP, if they have owned and lived in their Burlington home for at least a year.
intakeNote: Apply online, by email to propertytaxprograms@burlington.ca, or in person at City Hall by December 31; reapply each year (2026 applications are open now).

name: Burlington Transit Handi-Van
description: The City of Burlington's door-to-door Handi-Van service takes people who cannot use a regular bus anywhere in Burlington, including medical appointments and shopping. Fares are the same as the conventional bus, paid by PRESTO or cash, and adults 65 and over ride Burlington's conventional buses free with a PRESTO card.
intakeNote: Apply with the specialized transit form signed by a health care professional (reviewed within 14 days); once approved, book up to two weeks ahead at 905-639-5158 or online at hvbooking.burlington.ca.

name: Fair Entry and Recreation Fee Assistance (Calgary)
description: A City of Calgary program where one Fair Entry application lets lower-income Calgarians, including seniors, use city services at a reduced cost. Recreation Fee Assistance lowers the price of city pools, fitness centres, golf courses, classes and partner facilities, and the same application also covers the low-income transit pass and the Property Tax Assistance Program.
intakeNote: Apply online, by mail, or in person at a Fair Entry location (appointments can be booked online); one application a year covers all Fair Entry programs. Call 311 with questions.

name: Calgary Property Tax Assistance Program
description: A City of Calgary program that gives lower-income homeowners, including many seniors, a credit for the year-over-year increase on their property tax bill. It runs through the same Fair Entry application as other city subsidies, and is separate from the Alberta government's Seniors Property Tax Deferral loan.
intakeNote: Apply through Fair Entry between June 1 and December 31; call 311 (403-268-2489 from outside Calgary) with questions. Processing takes about 4 to 6 weeks.

name: Parks and Recreation Seniors Programs (City of Charlottetown)
description: The City of Charlottetown's Parks and Recreation Department publishes a seasonal program brochure with something for everyone from preschoolers to seniors, including seniors fitness classes delivered directly by the department. New brochures come out each spring and fall, and you can register online or by phone. It is a City of Charlottetown service.
intakeNote: Browse the seasonal Parks and Recreation program brochure on charlottetown.ca, then register online through the city's registration system or call 902-368-1025.

name: Leisure Access Program (Edmonton)
description: A City of Edmonton program that gives lower-income Edmontonians, including seniors, free or discounted entry to city recreation centres, pools and attractions, plus 75 percent off registered programs. The same application is automatically considered for the Ride Transit Program's discounted monthly bus pass. Any senior can also use the Senior Matinee Hour, $3.50 admission to city fitness centres, pools and gyms on weekdays from 11:30am to 1pm.
intakeNote: Complete the combined Leisure Access and Ride Transit application and submit it with income documents by mail, at the Edmonton Service Centre, or at a city recreation centre; emailed applications are not accepted. Call 311 for help.

name: Assisted Waste Collection (Edmonton)
description: A City of Edmonton service where collection staff pick up garbage and recycling from outside the front or back door for residents who cannot move their carts to the curb or lane. It covers temporary or long-term mobility challenges, at no extra charge.
intakeNote: Have a healthcare professional sign the program form, then apply online or call 311 (780-442-5311 outside Edmonton); staff contact you within about 10 business days to arrange a home visit.

name: Fredericton Senior Centre and Seniors Recreation
description: The Fredericton Senior Centre is owned and run by the City of Fredericton as a home base for activities and events for adults 50 and over. The city also offers free Senior Skates for 65+, seniors swims with $2.80 pool admission for 60+, free indoor walking tracks at the Grant Harvey Centre and Willie O'Ree Place, and a free Wednesday walking club from May to October.
intakeNote: Call Service Fredericton at 506-460-2020 to get started with any city program.

name: Vulnerable Persons Registry (Fredericton Police)
description: The Vulnerable Persons Registry is a free City of Fredericton police program that keeps vital information and a photo of a vulnerable person on file, so officers can respond quickly and gently if that person goes missing or needs help. Families caring for someone with Alzheimer's disease or another condition that leads to wandering or communication difficulty can register their loved one, and people can also register themselves.
intakeNote: Print and complete the registration form with a colour photo and mail or drop it off at the Fredericton Police Force, 311 Queen Street; renew each year.

name: Para Transit (Fredericton Transit)
description: Para Transit is the City of Fredericton's door-to-door accessible bus service for people whose disabilities keep them from riding regular Fredericton Transit buses. A separate fleet of accessible vehicles runs seven days a week, and regular riders can set up standing bookings for things like dialysis or day programs. Register through Service Fredericton, then book trips a day ahead by phone or app.
intakeNote: Apply through Service Fredericton at 506-460-2020 with the Para Transit Registration and Consent Form; once registered, call 506-460-2212 to book rides.

name: Macassa Lodge Adult Day Program
description: A daily adult day program run by the City of Hamilton at Macassa Lodge, its municipal long-term care home on the Mountain. Seniors enjoy social, recreational and physical activities in a supervised group, with a hot lunch, medication reminders and help with daily living, while family caregivers get a regular break.
intakeNote: Call Macassa Lodge at 905-546-2800 or email macassalodge@hamilton.ca to ask about joining the Adult Day Program.

name: Hamilton Recreation Assistance Program (RAP)
description: A City of Hamilton program that cuts recreation costs for residents living with a low income. Approved seniors choose 75% off an annual participation or skating pass, or 50% off Waterfit passes, valid for 12 months.
intakeNote: Apply online with proof of home address and family net income, such as a Notice of Assessment; email rap@hamilton.ca or call 905-546-2424 ext. 4569 for help.

name: Seniors' Centre Without Walls (Hamilton)
description: A free City of Hamilton recreation program that runs entirely over the phone, so older adults can join trivia, brain games, armchair travel and friendly chat sessions from home. Any phone works, calls average 5 to 10 people, and no special equipment is needed.
intakeNote: Call 905-526-4084 or email scww@hamilton.ca to register and get the current program schedule.

name: Hamilton Seniors Centres and 55+ Recreation Programs
description: City of Hamilton seniors centres and clubs offering drop-in and registered fitness, arts and social programs for adults 55 and over. The main centres are the Ancaster Seniors Achievement Centre, Sackville Hill Seniors Recreation Centre and Flamborough Seniors Centre, with smaller seniors clubs across the city.
intakeNote: Call 905-546-3747 for the three main senior centres, or browse and register through the city's online Program Finder.

name: Hamilton Funeral, Burial and Cremation Assistance
description: City of Hamilton financial help toward a basic funeral, burial or cremation when a Hamilton resident dies without enough money in their estate to cover it. The family member or friend handling arrangements must contact the city before signing any funeral home contract, because costs cannot be repaid afterward.
intakeNote: Call Special Supports at 905-546-2590 right after the death, and before signing anything with a funeral home or cemetery.

name: Ontario Renovates Hamilton (Home Repair Loans)
description: A home repair program delivered by the City of Hamilton that gives low income homeowners a forgivable loan of up to $25,000 for major structural, electrical, plumbing, heating or fire safety repairs, with a second stream for accessibility changes for people with disabilities. Stay in the home for 10 years and the loan is fully forgiven.
intakeNote: Call 905-546-2424 ext. 2758 or email affordablehousing@hamilton.ca for information or a paper application.

name: Hamilton Snow Clearing Subsidy (Snow Angels)
description: A City of Hamilton subsidy that pays seniors and residents with disabilities up to $450 each winter to hire help clearing snow from their sidewalk and the path to their front door. Applications are accepted each snow season from November 1 to March 31, or until the program is full.
intakeNote: Apply online or submit the paper form in person, by mail or by fax starting November 1; call 905-546-2590 to have a paper application mailed to you.

name: Hamilton Seniors (65+) Tax Rebate
description: A City of Hamilton rebate that takes $241 off the yearly property tax bill of low income homeowners aged 65 and over, plus an extra $175 Seniors Utility Rebate if the home has a metered water account. Once approved, you stay enrolled each year without reapplying.
intakeNote: Complete the Seniors Tax Rebate application and submit it in person at City Hall or a Municipal Service Centre, or by mail, by the last business day of February of the following year; emailed applications are no longer accepted. Call 905-546-2489 with questions.

name: Hamilton Property Tax Deferral for Seniors
description: City of Hamilton programs that let low income seniors and people on disability benefits put off paying property tax until the home is sold. You can defer just the yearly tax increase with no interest, or defer the full tax bill with interest and an application fee. The city also accepts compassionate appeals for tax relief in cases of extreme sickness or poverty.
intakeNote: Complete the deferral application and submit it by mail or in person at City Hall or a Municipal Service Centre; a new application is required each year. Call 905-546-2489 with questions.

name: Hamilton Special Supports Program
description: A City of Hamilton program that pays for health related equipment and services for residents with low incomes, including grab bars, bath and toilet aids, canes and walkers, emergency response systems, eyeglasses, dentures, taxi rides to medical appointments and adult day program fees. Apply before buying anything, because items already purchased cannot be funded.
intakeNote: Apply through the online Special Supports benefits application; a note or prescription from a doctor or health professional is usually required. Call 905-546-2590 or email support@hamilton.ca with questions.

name: Elder's Qammaq
description: The Elder's Qammaq is a City of Iqaluit drop-in centre where Elders gather to socialize, join organized activities, and mark special events. Afternoons bring a cooking club, workshops, and arts and crafts, in a recently renovated space run by the city's Recreation Department.
intakeNote: Call Recreation Reception at (867) 979-5611 or email recreation@iqaluit.ca; elders can simply drop in on weekday afternoons.

name: Financial Assistance for Recreation (Kelowna)
description: A City of Kelowna program that gives residents with low incomes, including seniors, a credit toward a Parkinson Recreation Centre pass or city recreation programs, such as the Move for your Health exercise classes for people with chronic health conditions. Separately, the city offers a reduced rate on admission and fitness classes for customers 65 and older who show a Pharmacare card.
intakeNote: Email accesstorecreation@kelowna.ca to apply; assessment takes up to two weeks. Questions: 250-469-8759, or visit the Access to Recreation Office in Parkinson Recreation Centre (Tuesday 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., Wednesday 4 p.m. to 7 p.m.).

name: Dearness Home Adult Day Program
description: A City of London adult day program at the Dearness Home, the city's own long-term care home. It runs Monday to Friday for seniors coping with frailty, disability or chronic illness, and the program fee covers help with personal care, all recreation and a three course lunch, with rides to and from the program available for an extra fee.
intakeNote: Call the City of London at 519-661-2489 (or 3-1-1 inside London) and ask for the Dearness Home Adult Day Program to check space availability and current fees.

name: London Recreation Fee Subsidy
description: A City of London subsidy that lowers or fully covers recreation costs for residents in financial need, including seniors' centre memberships and program fees. Support can reach 100% of the cost depending on family income.
intakeNote: Call 519-661-5575 to apply; you will need documents showing your family income.

name: London Seniors' Centres and Satellites
description: City of London seniors centres offering fitness, arts and social programs for older adults at the Kiwanis and Hamilton Road seniors' community centres, plus nine smaller satellite locations for adults 55 and over across the city. Yearly memberships keep costs low, and a fee subsidy is available if money is tight.
intakeNote: Call the Kiwanis Seniors' Community Centre at 519-661-5740 or the Hamilton Road centre at 519-661-5758, or register online through the Play Your Way portal or by calling 519-661-5575.

name: Ontario Renovates London (Home Repair and Accessibility Funding)
description: A home repair program delivered by the City of London with federal and provincial funding. Homeowners aged 60 or older and people with disabilities with low to moderate incomes can get a 10 year forgivable loan of up to $25,000 for essential repairs or accessibility changes, and the first $5,000 of accessibility work is a grant. Applications for 2026 are open now, first come, first served.
intakeNote: Complete the 2026 Homeowner Application Package with photo ID, your CRA Notice of Assessment, property tax documents and three contractor estimates; call 519-661-2489 x7831 or email housingprograms@london.ca with questions.

name: Seniors in the City (City of Moncton seniors programs)
description: The City of Moncton runs a full slate of low-cost activities for older adults, including a monthly Seniors Social, free daily walking sessions at the Crossman Community Centre and Moncton Coliseum, tai chi, shuffleboard, seniors aquafit for $3, and skating by donation. A monthly Seniors in the City calendar pulls everything together, and seniors 65 and older also ride Codiac Transpo buses free every Wednesday. It is a City of Moncton service, with most activities drop-in.
intakeNote: Most activities are drop-in at city facilities; call 506-853-3333 or check the monthly Seniors in the City calendar on moncton.ca for times and locations.

name: Oshawa Public Libraries Visiting Library Services
description: Free monthly home delivery of books and other library materials from Oshawa Public Libraries, the City of Oshawa's library system, for residents who cannot visit a branch. Staff build a personalized selection each month and deliver to homes, long-term care centres and retirement residences.
intakeNote: Call (905) 579-6111 ext. 5267 or complete the Visiting Library Services application form online or at any branch.

name: Oshawa Grass Cutting Assistance Program
description: A City of Oshawa service that cuts the side boulevard of corner lots for seniors 65 and over and people with disabilities, up to thirteen times a season from May to mid-October. It covers only the city-owned side boulevard, not the front boulevard or private lawn.
intakeNote: Complete the application and submit it to Service Oshawa; renew before April 1 each year.

name: Oshawa Snow Clearing Assistance Program
description: A free City of Oshawa service that clears the city sidewalk and the windrow, the pile of snow a plow leaves at the end of the driveway, for seniors 65 and over and people with disabilities who have no one in the home able to shovel. Service starts after snowfalls of more than 2.5 cm.
intakeNote: Apply online starting September 1 for the winter season; renew each year (renewal notices go out in October).

name: Oshawa Property Tax Grant for Low-Income Seniors
description: A City of Oshawa grant that lowers the property tax bill for senior homeowners with low incomes. If you are 65 or older, receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement and have owned and lived in your Oshawa home for at least a year, the grant is credited straight to your tax account. Homeowners receiving ODSP also qualify.
intakeNote: Apply between January 1 and April 30 each year, online or in person at Taxation Services, Oshawa City Hall, 50 Centre St. S.

name: City of Ottawa Adult Day Programs
description: Adult Day Programs at the City of Ottawa's Carleton Lodge and Centre d'accueil Champlain long term care homes give seniors living with dementia or other barriers a welcoming place to spend the day with activities and social time, and give family caregivers a regular break.
intakeNote: Apply through Ontario Health atHome for the Champlain region by calling 310-2222, no area code needed.

name: Ottawa Hand in Hand recreation fee support
description: A City of Ottawa subsidy that gives each qualifying resident $185 a year toward recreation and culture programs, so cost does not keep seniors from fitness classes, swimming or social programs. Seniors who receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement qualify, along with several other routes.
intakeNote: Fill out the Hand in Hand application, online or at any staffed recreation facility, and bring it to your local recreation or cultural facility; call 3-1-1 with questions.

name: City of Ottawa funeral and burial help (EHSS)
description: Through its Essential Health and Social Supports program, the City of Ottawa helps pay cremation and burial costs when a low income resident dies and their estate and family cannot cover a basic funeral. Families should call before finalizing arrangements with a funeral home.
intakeNote: Call 3-1-1 Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., press 1 for English then 4 for Community and Social Services, before making funeral arrangements.

name: City of Ottawa Home Support Services
description: A City of Ottawa service that provides light housekeeping, including floors, bathrooms, laundry and kitchen cleaning, for low income residents who have a medical reason they cannot do the work themselves and little or no other help. A case worker confirms eligibility with a phone interview and a home visit.
intakeNote: Call 3-1-1 Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., press 1 for English then 4 for Community and Social Services.

name: Snow Go and Snow Go Assist
description: A City of Ottawa program that matches older adults and people with disabilities with a screened person or contractor to clear snow from private driveways and walkways at an affordable rate. Snow Go Assist also pays up to half the cost for lower income households, to a seasonal maximum of $250, or $450 in rural areas where costs run higher.
intakeNote: Applications for each winter open in the fall through neighbourhood community support agencies; call 3-1-1 or your local community support agency to sign up before the snow flies.

name: Essential Health and Social Supports (EHSS)
description: A City of Ottawa program that pays for essentials low income residents cannot afford, including urgent dental care, dentures, eye exams and glasses, part of the cost of assistive devices, bathroom aids, surgical supplies, and help with rent or utility arrears. A case worker assesses eligibility in a phone or in-person interview.
intakeNote: Call 3-1-1 Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., press 1 for English then 4 for Community and Social Services.

name: Ottawa property tax deferral for low-income seniors
description: A City of Ottawa program that lets low income seniors and people with disabilities put off paying all or part of their property taxes until the home is sold, with a matching deferral program for water bills. For 2026 the home must be assessed under $498,000 and gross household income under about $59,400; deferred amounts carry 5 percent yearly interest.
intakeNote: Apply online, email taxdeferralprogram@ottawa.ca, or call Revenue Services at 613-580-2444 (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.); renewals are due by September 30 each year.

name: Para Transpo (OC Transpo accessible door-to-door transit)
description: The City of Ottawa's shared ride public transit service for people whose disability keeps them from using regular buses, run by OC Transpo with minibuses and contracted taxis. Riders apply once, then reserve trips at least a day ahead by phone or online through My Para Transpo.
intakeNote: Apply online or with the application form on octranspo.com; once registered, book trips at 613-560-5000 (TTY via 7-1-1), online through My Para Transpo, or text 57272 with questions.

name: Pickering 55+ Recreation Services
description: The City of Pickering runs low-cost recreation and social programming just for adults 55 and over: group fitness, free Spotlight seminars, club activities like euchre and tai chi, band nights and an annual Aging Well information fair. Adults over 65 get half off memberships at the Chestnut Hill Developments Recreation Complex.
intakeNote: Register online at pickering.ca/active, or call the 55+ recreation coordinator at 905-420-4660 ext. 6104.

name: Pickering Seniors and Persons with Disabilities Snow Clearing Program
description: A City of Pickering program that arranges seasonal snow clearing at home for residents 65 and over and people with disabilities, running November 1 to April 30. The fee is based on income: free for seniors receiving GAINS, then a sliding scale starting at about $129 for the season.
intakeNote: Apply online through forms.pickering.ca (form CSD2203) or call Customer Care at 905.683.7575; the program has 750 spots and applications are taken until full.

name: Pickering Tax Grant for Low Income Seniors
description: A City of Pickering grant of $620 in 2026 that is credited to the property tax account of senior homeowners with low incomes, offsetting the final September tax instalment. The city also runs a companion tax deferral program for the same group.
intakeNote: Apply by August 19 each year with the online form (FIN 1701) plus supporting documents, or by mail or drop-off at Pickering City Hall; reapply annually.

name: Red Deer Fee Assistance Program
description: A City of Red Deer program that helps residents facing financial challenges, including seniors on a low income, use city recreation facilities and programs. Approved members get a Recreation Pass Card for drop-in visits and up to $200 a year toward program registrations, and they also qualify for the city's $34 a month Transit Fare Assistance bus pass.
intakeNote: Bring your qualifying documents, government ID and proof of residence to customer service at the Collicutt Centre, G.H. Dawe Community Centre, Don Moore Recreation Centre or Michener Aquatic Centre for same-day enrollment, or apply online with your CRA Notice of Assessment; call 403-309-8411 or email feeassistance@reddeer.ca.

name: Red Deer Action Bus
description: Red Deer Transit's door-to-door shared ride bus, a City of Red Deer service for trips that cannot be made on regular transit because of a physical or cognitive disability. Lift-equipped buses carry registered riders across the city, with trips booked up to 14 days ahead.
intakeNote: Call 403-309-8400 to ask about the Action Bus and request the application form, or download it from the city website; all riders must be registered clients before booking.

name: Affordable Access Program
description: A City of Regina program that cuts the cost of staying active for residents with low incomes, including seniors. Approval brings 50 percent off single admissions, 80 percent off leisure passes and registered classes, and a 20 percent discount on adult transit passes.
intakeNote: Send the application form and income verification to affordableaccess@regina.ca or drop it off at the North West Leisure Centre, Sportplex, or Sandra Schmirler Leisure Centre; approval lasts to the end of the year and you re-apply annually.

name: Water, Waste and Municipal Tax Affordability Programs
description: A City of Regina program for low income households that include a senior or a person with a disability. One application covers two kinds of help: deferring 600 or 1,200 dollars of municipal property tax, or the yearly increase, until the home is sold, plus monthly rebates of roughly 25 dollars on water and 4.50 dollars on waste bills, doubled for very low incomes.
intakeNote: Send the affordability application form with your CRA Notice of Assessment and ID to APRSprograms@regina.ca or apply in person at City Hall or a leisure centre; tax deferral applications for 2026 close August 1.

name: Regina Paratransit
description: Regina Paratransit is a City of Regina shared ride, door-to-door bus service for people whose disability keeps them from consistently using the regular bus, including riders at risk of falling or who tire easily. Winter-only registration is available for people who manage fine in summer but not on ice and snow. Fares and passes match regular Regina Transit.
intakeNote: Register with the online Paratransit Application Form or call 306-777-7726 for help; once approved, book trips at 306-777-7007.

name: Leisure Access Program
description: A City of Saskatoon program that lets residents with low incomes, including seniors, use city leisure centres free of charge. An approved Leisure Access Card gives unlimited entry to drop-in programs plus one registered recreation program each year, and the same application can also unlock a discounted low income bus pass.
intakeNote: Apply online or with a paper form from any indoor leisure centre, attaching last year's CRA Notice of Assessment and proof of your Saskatoon address; decisions come by email in three to six weeks.

name: Seniors Property Tax Deferral Program
description: A City of Saskatoon program that lets homeowners 65 and older with low incomes put off paying some or all of the city and library portion of their property taxes so rising bills do not push them out of their home. One option simply freezes the yearly amount, and the deferred taxes are repaid only when the home is sold or transferred.
intakeNote: Apply fresh each year by October 31 using the current application form, available at City Hall, leisure centres, and libraries or mailed on request; call 306-975-2400 for help.

name: Saskatoon Access Transit
description: Access Transit is the City of Saskatoon's shared ride, door-to-door bus service for people whose temporary or permanent disability keeps them from using the regular bus. Lift-equipped buses run seven days a week within Saskatoon, and trips can be booked by phone up to seven days ahead. Regular Saskatoon Transit fares apply.
intakeNote: Register first: submit application Part A plus Part B completed by your health care practitioner, by email or mail; call 306-975-3555 with questions or to book trips once registered.

name: Seniors' Programs 50+ (City of St. John's Recreation)
description: The City of St. John's runs a year-round lineup for adults 50 and over: Active for Life fall prevention fitness, Social Time afternoons at rec centres, Lifelong Learners courses, and summer bus tours around the Avalon Peninsula with lunch and admission included. A Seniors in the Community stream brings gentle fitness and games right into seniors' apartment buildings so transportation is not a barrier. Register online through RECconnect or by phone.
intakeNote: Each program has its own line: 709-576-8251 for the seniors tax reduction, 709-576-8594 for seniors programs and bus tours, 709-576-8684 for the recreation subsidy.

name: Recreation Financial Support (adult program subsidy)
description: This City of St. John's program pays part or all of the cost of city recreation programs for residents who could not otherwise afford them, including older adults on fixed incomes. Support is based on income using Statistics Canada's low income cut-off. Apply any time with proof of residency and your CRA Notice of Assessment; decisions take 7 to 10 business days.
intakeNote: Each program has its own line: 709-576-8251 for the seniors tax reduction, 709-576-8594 for seniors programs and bus tours, 709-576-8684 for the recreation subsidy.

name: Seniors Tax Reduction (City of St. John's)
description: The City of St. John's reduces the property tax bill for lower-income senior homeowners. You qualify if you are 65 or older and receive the federal Guaranteed Income Supplement, or 60 to 64 and receive the Allowance for the Survivor, and the home is registered in your name as your main residence. Apply to the city with a confirmation letter from Service Canada.
intakeNote: Complete the Senior Citizens Tax Reduction Application and include a Government of Canada letter confirming GIS or Allowance for the Survivor (request one at 1-800-277-9914); questions to 709-576-8251.

name: City of Toronto Adult Day Programs
description: A City of Toronto service offering seniors a safe, social day out with activities, meals and wellness programming, Monday to Friday. It supports seniors who are frail, living with memory loss or socially isolated, and gives family caregivers a regular break.
intakeNote: Call the location nearest you: Bendale Acres in Scarborough 416-397-7020, Cummer Lodge in North York 416-392-9502, Kipling Acres in Etobicoke 416-392-2299. A program agreement is signed before the first day.

name: City of Toronto funeral support for people in financial need
description: A City of Toronto program that covers basic funeral, burial or cremation costs for Toronto residents who die without enough money in their estate, when family cannot pay. Families should call before finalizing arrangements with a funeral home.
intakeNote: Call 416-338-8888 and select option 4 before making funeral arrangements.

name: Homemakers and Nurses Services (City of Toronto)
description: A City of Toronto service, funded with the Province of Ontario, that sends a homemaker to help with light housekeeping, laundry, grocery shopping and meal preparation. It is for residents with limited income and assets who cannot manage these tasks on their own, and seniors are given priority.
intakeNote: Call 416-392-8579 to start a referral; an intake caseworker screens by phone, then visits the home to assess finances and need. There is a wait list.

name: Toronto Community Paramedicine Program
description: A City of Toronto service where specially trained paramedics visit seniors at home to check blood pressure and medications, spot safety risks, and connect them with health and community supports. It helps seniors who call 911 often or who struggle to reach regular care, and includes homebound vaccinations in fall and winter.
intakeNote: Clients and caregivers can self-refer: call 416-397-4322 and press option 1, or email cphome@toronto.ca.

name: City of Toronto Supportive Housing Program for seniors
description: A City of Toronto service, funded by Ontario Health, that places personal support workers inside nine designated seniors apartment buildings. Tenants get help with personal care, light housekeeping, laundry, medication reminders and safety checks, with on-site staff available around the clock.
intakeNote: Tenants of a designated building can call 416-397-7400 or visit the Supportive Housing office in their building; others first need a unit in one of the nine buildings through social housing.

name: Toronto Hardship Fund (help with health expenses)
description: A City of Toronto fund that pays for health items low-income residents cannot afford, including eyeglasses and eye exams, emergency dental work and dentures, prescription medications, walkers, hearing aids and hospital beds. It serves people who are not on Ontario Works or ODSP, regardless of immigration status.
intakeNote: Call 416-338-8888 and select option 3. Apply before paying for the item, because purchases made first may not be reimbursed.

name: Property Tax, Water and Solid Waste Relief Programs
description: A City of Toronto program that cancels or defers property tax increases and rebates part of water and garbage bills for low-income seniors and low-income people with disabilities who own their home. Applications for the 2026 tax year are open until November 2, 2026.
intakeNote: Apply online each year (the CRA verifies income automatically) or send a paper form by mail; call 311 with questions.

name: Arts & Health: Healthy Aging through the Arts
description: A Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation program, run with Vancouver Coastal Health, where professional artists lead weekly arts workshops for seniors and Elders at community sites across the city. Groups dance, sing, write, paint and weave together for about 30 weeks between October and June, with a year-end showcase of their work.
intakeNote: Call the Park Board's community arts programmer at 604-404-8273 or email info@artsandhealth.ca to find a participating site near you.

name: Leisure Access Program (Vancouver)
description: A City of Vancouver program that gives low-income residents, including seniors, free or reduced-cost access to Park Board pools, ice rinks, fitness centres and community centre programs. Passes issued in 2026 are valid for 3 years.
intakeNote: Fill out the self-refer application form from the program page and submit it with proof of income; questions go to lap@vancouver.ca, or phone the city at 3-1-1.

name: Snow Angels (Vancouver)
description: A City of Vancouver program that matches seniors and people with limited mobility with volunteer neighbours who clear the snow and ice from their sidewalk. When snow is sticking, phone 3-1-1 and the city will try to connect you with a Snow Angel in your area.
intakeNote: Phone 3-1-1 to request a Snow Angel when it is snowing and sticking at least 1 centimetre on the sidewalk.

name: L.I.F.E. Program (Victoria)
description: A City of Victoria program that gives residents with low incomes, including seniors, a free two year pass with unlimited drop-ins at Crystal Pool and Fitness Centre, free public skating at Save-On-Foods Memorial Arena, and 52 drop-in visits a year at partner recreation centres around the region. Pass holders also get a program credit and can buy an annual Regional Recreation Pass at half price.
intakeNote: Submit the L.I.F.E. application form with proof of residency (a recent bill or rental agreement) and your CRA Notice of Assessment; applications go through Crystal Pool and Fitness Centre, 250.361.0732.

name: Senior Utility Rebate
description: A City of Whitehorse rebate that pays seniors back for city utility bills. Residents 65 and older, and qualifying surviving spouses, can get up to 500 dollars a year back on water, sewer, and curbside collection fees for their home.
intakeNote: Apply with the city's rebate form at City Hall, 2121 Second Avenue, during the annual application window; processing takes two to three weeks, and 867-667-6401 can confirm current dates and amounts.

name: Handy Bus
description: The Handy Bus is the City of Whitehorse's accessible door-to-door bus, funded with the Yukon government, for people who have difficulty riding the regular bus. It runs seven days a week on both a scheduled and casual basis, with weekend trips booked by Friday afternoon.
intakeNote: Complete the application form, including the medical provider section, and drop it at City Hall or the Whitehorse Transit office at 187 Range Road; approval word comes within 15 business days, then book at 867-668-8394.

name: Winnipeg Public Library Home Service
description: A City of Winnipeg library service that brings books, audiobooks, large print, movies, and magazines each month to Winnipeggers who cannot get to a branch because of long-term illness or disability. Staff learn your tastes and pick titles for you. A companion Selection Service at 204-986-6489 chooses audiobooks and large print for pickup at any branch.
intakeNote: Call the Home Service Coordinator at 204-986-2738 at the Millennium Library to get started.

name: Recreation Fee Assistance Program
description: A City of Winnipeg program that helps residents with low incomes stay active at city recreation centres. Approved adults, including seniors, get a free pass for city pools and fitness centres plus a 300 dollar yearly credit for registered programs like aquafit and skating.
intakeNote: Send the application form and proof of income to RecFeeAssist@winnipeg.ca, or drop it off at 395 Main St. or any indoor pool or fitness centre; call 311 with questions.

name: Boulevard snow clearing for residents with disabilities
description: A City of Winnipeg public works service that clears a 1.5 metre path through boulevard snow between the curb and the sidewalk after major snowfalls, so approved residents can safely reach a vehicle at the street. It is meant for homeowners with no front driveway who cannot shovel for medical reasons and cannot afford to hire help.
intakeNote: Apply with the city form plus a medical professional's verification by email to PWD-Customer-Service@winnipeg.ca or by mail to the Public Works Customer Service Branch.

name: Access for All
description: A City of Yellowknife program that gives residents with low incomes, including seniors, free city transit and free drop-in recreation. Approved households get a three-year pass covering YKTransit, YKFlex, and public drop-in activities at the ATCO Aquatic Centre, Multiplex, and Fieldhouse.
intakeNote: Drop the application form and your GNWT Income Assistance report or CRA Notice of Assessment at City Hall, or email it; call (867) 920-5686 with questions.

name: Senior and Disabled Tax Relief
description: A City of Yellowknife rebate of up to 2,000 dollars a year on property tax for homeowners who are 65 or older, or living with a disability, and who own and live in the home. You apply each year with the city's Tax Relief Form, and rebates are not granted for past years.
intakeNote: Download the Tax Relief Form from yellowknife.ca or pick one up at City Hall, attach the supporting documents, and submit annually; call 867-920-5600 weekdays 8 to 4:30.

name: YKFlex accessible transit (formerly YATS)
description: YKFlex is the City of Yellowknife's door-to-door bus service, formerly called YATS, for registered riders whose disability keeps them from using the regular bus safely. Trips run Monday to Saturday and can be booked up to seven days ahead. Registered riders and seniors 60 and older pay discounted transit fares.
intakeNote: Complete the YKFlex application form, have a health care professional sign it, and submit it to the NWT Disabilities Council; once approved, book trips at (867) 873-8901, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. weekdays and Saturdays.

name: CMHA Durham Case Management and Community Services
description: A registered charity offering one-to-one mental health case management and support in Durham Region, including recovery and crisis planning, medication management, life skills help, and family or caregiver support. This is a community mental health service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call, email, walk in, or use the online form at cmhadurham.ca/client-intake/ to reach Community Connection Services, the intake team that assesses anyone in Durham Region and refers them into Case Management and Community Services or other CMHA Durham programs; there is no separate senior-only intake line.

name: CMHA Toronto Grief Support Program
description: A registered charity's free, drop-in grief support group, held weekly online and facilitated by a registered psychotherapist. Open to adults grieving any kind of loss, including seniors coping with the loss of a spouse, friends, or independence, and to caregivers supporting someone who is grieving.
intakeNote: Call 416-789-7957 or email info@cmhato.org to ask about any CMHA Toronto program, or self-refer straight into the Grief Support Program with its online registration form (no professional referral needed).

name: CNIB Tech
description: A registered charity that helps Canadians who are blind or partially sighted use accessible technology, through free group and one-to-one training, smartphone apps, and devices like a free smartphone for registered clients. This is a national charity program, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call the national line or fill out the online contact form at cnib.ca to reach a CNIB program coordinator, who can register you and connect you to programs like Tech and Peer Support, or point you to a referral for vision loss rehabilitation training.

name: Community Care Durham Friendly Visiting
description: A registered charity that matches Durham Region seniors and adults with disabilities to a volunteer for regular, friendly social visits, usually about once a week. This is a free non-profit community service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call 1-888-255-6680 or fill out the online Request Service form on communitycaredurham.on.ca to book an appointment with a Central Intake Coordinator; the Adult Day Program additionally requires a separate referral from Ontario Health atHome (905-430-3308).

name: Community Care Durham Personal Support (Caregiver Relief) In-Home Respite
description: A registered charity providing in-home respite through Personal Support Workers, who give personal care, help with daily living, meal preparation, and light housekeeping so family caregivers in Durham Region can take a break. This is a non-profit community service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call 1-888-255-6680 or fill out the online Request Service form on communitycaredurham.on.ca to book an appointment with a Central Intake Coordinator; the Adult Day Program additionally requires a separate referral from Ontario Health atHome (905-430-3308).

name: Community Care Durham Meals on Wheels
description: A registered charity delivering hot and frozen meals across Durham Region, with volunteers who also do a friendly safety check at the door. Meal options include Halal, vegetarian, low sodium, gluten-free, minced, and pureed. This is a non-profit community service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call 1-888-255-6680 or fill out the online Request Service form on communitycaredurham.on.ca to book an appointment with a Central Intake Coordinator; the Adult Day Program additionally requires a separate referral from Ontario Health atHome (905-430-3308).

name: Community Care Durham WeConnect Mental Health and Wellness
description: A registered charity running WeConnect, formerly called COPE Mental Health, a free community mental health program across Durham Region with support groups, workshops, and educational sessions for people 16 and older. This is a non-profit community service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call 1-888-255-6680 or fill out the online Request Service form on communitycaredurham.on.ca to book an appointment with a Central Intake Coordinator; the Adult Day Program additionally requires a separate referral from Ontario Health atHome (905-430-3308).

name: Community Care Durham Transportation
description: A registered charity offering accessible van rides, volunteer drivers, and PSW-escorted medical rides for people in Durham Region who cannot use public transportation because of age or health needs. This is a non-profit community service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Call 1-888-255-6680 or fill out the online Request Service form on communitycaredurham.on.ca to book an appointment with a Central Intake Coordinator; the Adult Day Program additionally requires a separate referral from Ontario Health atHome (905-430-3308).

name: ConnexOntario Mental Health and Addiction Helpline
description: A free 24/7 helpline funded by the Government of Ontario and Ontario Health that finds mental health, addiction and problem gambling services anywhere in the province. Staff look up local options with you and connect you to the right program.
intakeNote: Call any time, text CONNEX to 247247, or use the live chat at connexontario.ca; no referral needed.

name: Benefits Finder (canada.ca)
description: A free Government of Canada online tool that asks a few quick questions and builds a personal list of federal benefits, with filters for seniors and retirees aged 60 and over and for caregivers. It needs no account or personal identifying information, and it links to your province's own benefits page too.
intakeNote: Use the tool online at benefitsfinder.services.gc.ca; for general help with federal programs call 1 800 O-Canada at 1-800-622-6232.

name: Tax credits for seniors and family caregivers (CRA)
description: Canada Revenue Agency credits that cut the tax bill for seniors and the relatives who support them, all claimed on the yearly tax return. They include the age amount for people 65 and older, pension income splitting with a spouse, the medical expense credit that covers attendant care and many home health costs, the Canada Caregiver Credit, the Home Accessibility Tax Credit for up to $20,000 a year of safety renovations, and the Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit, which refunds 14.5% of up to $50,000 spent adding a secondary suite for a senior.
intakeNote: Claim these credits when filing the yearly income tax return, or ask a tax preparer or free tax clinic to check each one; call the CRA with questions.

name: Disability Tax Credit (DTC)
description: A Government of Canada tax credit that lowers income tax for people with a severe, long-term impairment, or for the family member who supports them. Long-term conditions that affect everyday life, such as dementia, may qualify. Once approved, the credit can be claimed for past years going back up to 10 years, which can mean a large refund.
intakeNote: Apply using the CRA's digital DTC application or Form T2201 by mail; a medical practitioner completes the medical part, then the credit is claimed at tax time.

name: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB)
description: A tax-free Government of Canada payment every three months for people with low and modest incomes, which replaced the GST/HST credit in July 2026 with a 25% higher amount. There is no application; filing your tax return each year, even with no income, automatically signs you up if you qualify.
intakeNote: File a tax return every year to be enrolled automatically; call 1-800-387-1193 with payment questions.

name: Free tax clinics (Community Volunteer Income Tax Program)
description: Free tax clinics supported by the Canada Revenue Agency, where trained community volunteers complete tax returns for people with a modest income and a simple tax situation. Filing every year is what keeps benefits like the Guaranteed Income Supplement flowing, so these clinics matter even when no tax is owed. In Quebec the program runs jointly with Revenu Quebec as the Income Tax Assistance volunteer program.
