intakeNote: Find a nearby clinic with the Find a free tax clinic directory on canada.ca; clinic types and dates vary by community organization.

name: DARTS Accessible Transit (Hamilton)
description: The City of Hamilton's accessible transit service, a shared ride, door-to-door van service for people whose disability or health condition keeps them from using regular HSR buses. The city's Accessible Transportation Services office decides who qualifies, and DARTS operates the vehicles under contract. Fares are the same as regular HSR bus fares, which include senior rates.
intakeNote: Complete the ATS application form, with one section signed by a health care professional, and submit by mail, fax or email; call 905-529-1212 and press 1 for help. Once registered, book rides with DARTS at 905-529-1717.

name: Hamilton Taxi Scrip Program
description: A City of Hamilton program that sells subsidized taxi coupons to residents who qualify for DARTS accessible transit, giving them a flexible way to take taxis alongside their booked rides. Registered users carry an ATS photo ID card and show it when buying and spending the coupons.
intakeNote: Apply with the same ATS application form as DARTS, mailed to Accessible Transportation Services, c/o 71 Main St. West, Hamilton, ON L8P 4Y5; eligibility decisions take up to 14 days.

name: The Dorothy Ley Hospice
description: A registered charity offering hospice palliative care from a 12 suite residence in Etobicoke plus a home based palliative care team. It serves Etobicoke, west Toronto and part of east Mississauga. Both the residence and the home team need a doctor's referral, and both are free to patients and families.
intakeNote: A doctor faxes a referral form for the hospice residence or the home based palliative care team, but families can also call the main line or the 24 hour helpline to ask questions, and grief and bereavement support can be self-referred online without a doctor.

name: Durham Region Adult Day Programs
description: The Region of Durham runs supervised day programs for older adults at Hillsdale Estates in Oshawa, Lakeview Manor in Beaverton and Lakeridge Health Port Perry, with the Hillsdale program built for people living with dementia. Days include activities, exercise, a hot lunch and snacks, and give family caregivers a regular break.
intakeNote: Referrals go through Ontario Health atHome at 1-800-263-3877; for program questions call Hillsdale Estates at 905-579-1777 ext. 6318.
runBy: Region of Durham (seniors programs and Durham Region Transit)

name: Durham Region Community Paramedicine
description: A Region of Durham Paramedic Services program where specially trained paramedics visit people with high care needs at home, offering health checks, diagnostic testing, remote monitoring and help connecting to other services. The goal is to keep seniors well at home and out of the emergency department.
intakeNote: Intake is by referral from Ontario Health atHome, a family doctor or paramedic services; families can call 289-404-7034 with questions about a referral.

name: Durham Region Respite Care (short stays at Lakeview Manor)
description: The Region of Durham offers short respite stays of about one week to two months at Lakeview Manor, its long-term care home in Beaverton, so family caregivers can rest or travel. Short-stay residents receive the same care and services as long-stay residents, then return home.
intakeNote: Apply through Ontario Health atHome Central East at 905-430-3308 or 1-800-263-3877; Lakeview Manor's local line is 705-426-7388.

name: Durham Region Transit On Demand and Specialized Services
description: Durham Region Transit runs On Demand shared rides plus Specialized Transit, a door-to-door service for people whose disability keeps them from using the regular bus for all or part of a trip. It covers the whole region, including rural areas outside Oshawa, Whitby, Ajax and Pickering. Regular DRT fares apply, and seniors 65 and over pay a reduced fare with a PRESTO card.
intakeNote: Apply for Specialized Services with a form from durhamregiontransit.com (download or request by mail), then book trips with an agent at 1-866-247-0055 or 311.

name: Seniors Safety Line
description: A free, confidential helpline open 24 hours a day for older adults who are being abused, mistreated or feel unsafe, run by Elder Abuse Prevention Ontario with Ontario government support. Counsellors offer emotional support, safety planning and referrals to local services in over 200 languages (TTY 1-866-299-0008).
intakeNote: Call any time, day or night; a trained counsellor answers and no referral is needed.

name: DATS, Dedicated Accessible Transit Service
description: Edmonton Transit Service's door-to-door shared ride buses, a City of Edmonton service for residents who cannot use regular buses or the LRT for some or all trips because of a physical or cognitive disability. Registered riders book trips up to 3 days ahead by phone or online and pay regular transit fares.
intakeNote: Call 780-496-4567 and choose option 3 to check eligibility and register; DATS confirms which forms to send you. Registered riders book trips at the same number, option 2, or online.

name: EPL Home Delivery
description: A free service from Edmonton Public Library, the city's public library system, for people who cannot visit a branch for three months or more because of disability, illness or age. Library staff help pick out books, large print, DAISY and audio materials and deliver them right to the door, with longer loan periods, and EPL also serves extended care facilities and seniors lodges.
intakeNote: Call 780-496-7000 or contact your local branch to register; a friend or family member can also pick up chosen materials for you.

name: Access-A-Bus (Halifax Transit)
description: Access-A-Bus is Halifax Transit's shared ride, door-to-door bus service, a Halifax Regional Municipality program for people who cannot use regular transit because of a physical or cognitive disability. Apply with a form signed by a health professional, then book trips by phone up to 24 hours ahead for medical appointments, errands, and social outings. Seniors 65 and older also ride regular Halifax Transit buses and ferries free every Tuesday from 10 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and after 6 p.m.
intakeNote: Mail the three-part application form, with one section completed by a doctor, nurse practitioner, occupational therapist, or physiotherapist, to Halifax Transit; once registered, call 902-490-6999 to book trips.

name: Library Home Delivery and Borrow by Mail
description: Home Delivery is a free service from Halifax Public Libraries, the Halifax Regional Municipality's library system. If a disability, long-term illness, or caregiving duties keep you from getting to a branch, library staff or volunteers bring books, audiobooks, and other items to your door every three weeks, and can even pick titles based on your interests. People outside the delivery areas are signed up for Borrow by Mail instead, and nobody pays late fees.
intakeNote: Sign up online at halifaxpubliclibraries.ca, email hd@halifaxlibrary.ca, or call (902) 490-5725; no medical note is needed.

name: Recreation Access Program (subsidized recreation)
description: The Recreation Access Program is a Halifax Regional Municipality subsidy that covers 25, 50, or 100 percent of the cost of city recreation programs and rec centre memberships for residents in financial need, including older adults. Since January 2026 it also covers one-month memberships at the big multi-district facilities like the Canada Games Centre and Zatzman Sportsplex. Apply with proof of income before you pay for a program.
intakeNote: Call 311 (1-800-835-6428 outside Halifax) or send one Affordable Access Program application by email to AffordableAccess@halifax.ca, by mail, or in person at a municipal recreation centre or customer contact centre.

name: Property Tax Rebate, Deferral, and Payment Help (Affordable Access Program)
description: If the property tax bill is a struggle, Halifax Regional Municipality can pay part of it for you. This municipal program gives homeowners with a household income of $59,000 or less a rebate, and lets you defer the rest of the bill or switch to smaller monthly payments. The same Affordable Access application can also get you 50 percent off a monthly transit pass.
intakeNote: Call 311 (1-800-835-6428 outside Halifax) or send one Affordable Access Program application by email to AffordableAccess@halifax.ca, by mail, or in person at a municipal recreation centre or customer contact centre.

name: Voluntary Vulnerable Persons Registry
description: The Voluntary Vulnerable Persons Registry is a Halifax Regional Municipality emergency management list for residents who may need extra help during storms, long power outages, or evacuations. Seniors without round-the-clock support who have mobility, vision, hearing, or memory difficulties, or who rely on electricity for medical equipment, can join so emergency staff know to reach out and check on them.
intakeNote: Complete the online intake form on halifax.ca or call 311; the registry coordinator follows up within three days to confirm eligibility.

name: Halton Region Adult Day Programs
description: Halton Region runs three accredited adult day programs for older adults living with frail health, physical disability or dementia, with therapeutic activities, social time, personal care help and lunch. The sites are Silver Creek Place in Georgetown plus Milton Place and Friends Landing in Milton, and they serve families from across Halton, including Oakville and Burlington.
intakeNote: Call the Central Registry at 905-281-4443 (centralregistry.ca) to start; Ontario Health atHome clients can ask their care coordinator for a referral.

name: Halton Region Assisted Living and Supports for Daily Living
description: A Halton Region program giving seniors in designated buildings 24-hour access to personal support workers for bathing, dressing, medication help, meals, light housekeeping and safety checks, so they can keep living independently. Sites include Wellington Terrace and Bonnie Place in Burlington, the John R. Rhodes Residence in Oakville, and Martin House in Milton.
intakeNote: For Oakville and Milton sites call the Central Registry at 905-281-4443; for Burlington sites call Home and Community Care at 905-639-5228 or 1-800-810-0000.

name: Halton Assisted Wheeled Cart Waste Collection
description: With Halton Region's new wheeled cart garbage and recycling program, residents who cannot move the carts to the curb because of age or disability can be approved for assisted collection. The collection crew walks onto the property, takes the carts from a set spot beside or in front of the house, and returns them after pickup.
intakeNote: Call 311 to explain your circumstances; staff review each request and set up the assisted service.

name: Halton Older Adults Property Tax Deferral Program
description: A Halton Region program that lets older homeowners with modest incomes put off paying their full annual property taxes, interest free, as a loan repaid when the home is sold. It applies across Halton, including Milton and Halton Hills, and is handled by each local tax office.
intakeNote: Apply before September 30 with a recent Notice of Assessment at your local tax office: Oakville 905-845-6601, Burlington 905-335-7750; one-time $200 administration fee if approved.

name: Hamilton Public Library Home Library Service
description: A free Hamilton Public Library service, part of the City of Hamilton's library system, that mails books and other library materials to residents who cannot get to a branch. Staff pick items to match your interests, and returns go back in a postage paid envelope or with a family member at any branch.
intakeNote: Apply online or with a printable form from any branch; call 905-546-3200 x 3222 or email HLS@hpl.ca, and expect 4 to 6 weeks to the first delivery.

name: Hope for Wellness Help Line
description: A Government of Canada helpline offering free counselling and crisis support to all Indigenous people across Canada, 24 hours a day, with culturally grounded Indigenous counsellors. Support is available by phone in English and French, with Cree, Ojibway and Inuktitut on request, and by online chat at hopeforwellness.ca.
intakeNote: Call 1-855-242-3310 at any hour, or use the online chat at hopeforwellness.ca; no referral needed.

name: Hospice Mississauga
description: A registered charity that has provided community hospice care in Mississauga since 1985. Trained staff and volunteers visit people with a life limiting illness in their own homes and offer grief and bereavement support, including a youth program that also reaches grieving families in Brampton, all at no cost to patients and caregivers.
intakeNote: A family calls the Hospice Palliative Helpline at 905-667-1865 or fills out one of four online referral forms on the Hospice Mississauga site, no doctor referral needed.

name: Hospice Toronto In-Home Care
description: A registered charity that sends trained volunteers into a person's home to provide practical, emotional, and spiritual support for someone with a life-threatening illness, plus respite so family caregivers can rest. All services are free of charge.
intakeNote: Families and individuals can self-refer by calling the office at 416-364-1666; organizations refer using the Toronto Central Palliative Care Network Common Referral Form faxed to 416-364-2231.

name: Legal Aid Ontario
description: Ontario's provincial legal aid agency gives people with low incomes free legal help, including certificates that pay for a lawyer, duty counsel at court and a province-wide network of community legal clinics. One call checks what you qualify for, with service in over 300 languages.
intakeNote: Call Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., to check what you qualify for and be directed to the right service or local clinic.

name: London Public Library Visiting Library Service
description: A free London Public Library service, part of the City of London's library system, that brings library materials to residents who cannot get to a branch. Staff choose items to match your interests and deliver them to your home or long-term care residence each month, or send them to any branch for a family member or friend to pick up.
intakeNote: Complete the VLS application form online or at any branch; call 519-661-6444 (Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm) or email visiting.library@lpl.ca.

name: London Transit Specialized Transit
description: A shared ride, door-to-door transit service run by the London Transit Commission, the City of London's public transit agency, for Londoners whose disability keeps them from using regular buses on a regular basis. Registered riders also receive a pass for free travel on regular buses during off peak hours.
intakeNote: Complete the application form, with one section completed by a healthcare professional, and mail or drop it off at 450 Highbury Avenue North; call 519-451-1347 with questions. Once registered, book rides at 519-453-3444.

name: Health Links - Info Sante
description: Manitoba's government-funded provincial health advice line, answered by registered nurses 24 hours a day, every day. Call to talk through symptoms and get guidance on whether to treat at home, see a doctor, or go to emergency, in English or French with interpreters in more than 200 languages.
intakeNote: Just call any time: 204-788-8200 in Winnipeg or 1-888-315-9257 toll free.

name: Manitoba Pharmacare Program
description: A Government of Manitoba drug benefit for residents of any age whose income is seriously affected by high prescription drug costs. Once your income-based annual deductible is reached, eligible prescription drugs are covered for the rest of the benefit year, and since April 2025 the Enhanced Pharmacare Program also covers most diabetes and hormone replacement medications at no cost.
intakeNote: Enrol once with the Pharmacare Application and Consent Authorization Form so the Canada Revenue Agency can confirm your income each year; call 204-786-7141 or 1-800-297-8099 with questions.

name: Seniors Eyeglass Program
description: A Government of Manitoba benefit that helps seniors 65 and older with the cost of eyeglasses. It reimburses set amounts for dispensing fees, frames, and lenses after a $50 deductible, for one pair every three years or sooner if your prescription changes.
intakeNote: Pay for your glasses, then send in the claim form from your supplier, or ask the supplier to submit it for you; call 204-786-7365 or 204-786-7366 (toll free 1-800-297-8099 ext 7365 or 7366) with questions.

name: Manitoba Seniors Hearing Aid Program
description: A Government of Manitoba program that pays up to $2,000 toward hearing aids for seniors, including the hearing assessment and fitting. One claim can be made every five years, and the amount is applied right at the point of sale once you are approved.
intakeNote: Apply first, before buying: mail, fax, or drop off the application form with a CRA Proof of Income statement and a hearing assessment from a licensed Manitoba hearing aid dealer to Provincial Services in Winnipeg; call 204-945-5588 or 1-844-403-4327 (HEAR) with questions.

name: Manitoba Safe and Healthy Home for Seniors Program
description: A Government of Manitoba funded program, delivered by March of Dimes Canada, that pays up to $5,000 ($6,500 in rural and remote areas) for home accessibility and safety upgrades so seniors can stay in their homes longer. Grab bars, ramps, and other basic adaptations essential for daily living all qualify.
intakeNote: Apply through March of Dimes Canada online or call 1-866-906-6006 for help completing the application.

name: 55 PLUS Program (Manitoba Income Supplement)
description: A Government of Manitoba benefit that pays lower-income Manitobans aged 55 and over a supplement four times a year, currently up to $161.80 per quarter for a single person and $173.90 for each eligible person in a couple. It helps stretch a fixed income between pension cheques.
intakeNote: If you receive Old Age Security, eligibility is set automatically from your GIS or Allowance; otherwise mail or fax the printable application to Provincial Services any time of year, or call 204-948-7368 or 1-877-587-6224.

name: Primary Caregiver Tax Credit
description: A Government of Manitoba refundable tax credit of $1,400 a year for people who give unpaid care to a family member, neighbour, or friend living at home with significant care needs. It is not income tested, so caregivers can claim it even with no taxable income, helping cover costs like shopping, transport, and respite.
intakeNote: Register online or by paper form (a doctor or nurse practitioner completes the Level of Care Equivalency form if needed), then claim the credit on your income tax return; call the Manitoba Tax Assistance Office at 204-948-2115 or 1-800-782-0771 with questions.

name: Manitoba Seniors' Advocate
description: Manitoba's independent Seniors' Advocate, an office created by the Government of Manitoba that opened in November 2025. The advocate looks into the problems seniors and their families face with health care, housing, and government programs, and reports to the legislature with recommendations for change.
intakeNote: Call 204-583-0187 or email seniorsadvocate@seniorsadvocatemb.ca to raise a concern.

name: Seniors' School Tax Rebate
description: A Government of Manitoba rebate of up to $235 a year on the school taxes senior homeowners pay on their principal residence. It continues alongside the new Homeowners Affordability Tax Credit, which gives all homeowners up to $1,600 in school tax savings in 2026.
intakeNote: Claim it on your personal income tax return; for questions call the Manitoba Tax Assistance Office at 204-948-2115 or toll free 1-800-782-0771.

name: School Tax Assistance for Tenants 55 Plus (STAT 55+)
description: A Government of Manitoba rebate of up to $175 a year that helps renters aged 55 and over with the school tax portion of their rent. Lower-income tenants can even apply retroactively for up to four past years.
intakeNote: Mail or drop off the application form (printable or fillable versions online) to Provincial Services; call 204-948-7368 or 1-877-587-6224 with questions.

name: Protection for Persons in Care Office
description: A Government of Manitoba office that receives and investigates reports of abuse or neglect of adults in personal care homes, hospitals, and other designated health facilities. Families who are worried about how a loved one is being treated in care can report their concerns here.
intakeNote: Call 204-788-6366 in Winnipeg or 1-866-440-6366 toll free, or email protection@gov.mb.ca; in an emergency call 911 first and report to the office when safe.

name: Home and Vehicle Modification Program
description: An Ontario government funded program, delivered by March of Dimes Canada, that pays for basic home changes such as ramps, stair lifts and bathroom modifications so people whose mobility is limited can keep living safely at home. It covers up to $15,000 lifetime for home modifications and up to $15,000 every 10 years for vehicle modifications.
intakeNote: Download the application from marchofdimes.ca and mail it in with proof of income, disability verification and a vendor quote; call 1-877-369-4867 or email hvmp@marchofdimes.ca with questions.

name: Montreal Libraries Home Book Delivery
description: Free home delivery of library books, films and other items for people 65 and over or with limited mobility, a Ville de Montreal public library service (Bibliotheques de Montreal). Available in several boroughs; each borough library registers its own readers, so call 311 or check the city page to find the service in your area.
intakeNote: Call 311 (514 872-0311 from outside Montreal) or use the steps page at montreal.ca to find your borough library's home delivery contact and register; a library card is needed and can be set up at registration.

name: Seniors Active Living Centres
description: More than 400 local centre programs funded by the Ontario government where older adults join fitness classes, arts and culture programs, book clubs, social groups and lifelong learning, in person, online or by phone. Ontario has funded these centres for 60 years.
intakeNote: Use the online map to find the centre nearest you, then call that centre directly to join; the ministry's Seniors' INFOline at 1-888-910-1999 can also help you find one.

name: Seniors' INFOline
description: The Ontario government's free information line for anything to do with programs and services for seniors, from benefits and tax credits to housing, safety and community supports (TTY 1-800-387-5559). One call is often the fastest way to find out which provincial program fits your situation.
intakeNote: Call the Seniors' INFOline for anything to do with Ontario seniors programs; no referral needed.

name: Senior driver licence renewal at 80 and over
description: The Ontario government's renewal program that keeps drivers 80 and older safely on the road. Every 2 years you watch a short senior driver education video at home, then attend a booked appointment for a vision assessment and a 5 minute screening exercise; most drivers do not need a road test.
intakeNote: Wait for the renewal letter that arrives up to 90 days before the licence expires, then book online or call 1-800-396-4233 (416-235-3579 in the GTA), Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

name: Day Activity Services for Seniors
description: A Government of New Brunswick service where seniors spend the day in a group setting with planned social and recreational activities, meals, and gentle health monitoring, which also gives family caregivers a break. Access is arranged through a Social Development long-term care service plan.
intakeNote: Call Social Development at 1-833-733-7835; day activity services are added to a senior's long-term care service plan.

name: New Brunswick Drug Plans for Seniors
description: A Government of New Brunswick program that gives seniors prescription drug coverage. Seniors who receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement join the New Brunswick Prescription Drug Program, and other seniors can enrol in the New Brunswick Drug Plan, where premiums and co-payments are based on household income.
intakeNote: An application package is mailed automatically about 60 days before your 65th birthday; you can also call 1-800-332-3692 or mail the form to New Brunswick Drug Plans, PO Box 690, Moncton.

name: Tele-Care 811
description: A free, bilingual, and confidential Government of New Brunswick health line. Call 811 any time, day or night, to speak with a registered nurse who can assess symptoms, give advice, and book a virtual appointment with a nurse practitioner.
intakeNote: Dial 811 from anywhere in New Brunswick, 24 hours a day.

name: Health Services Hearing Aid Program
description: A Government of New Brunswick program that pays for hearing aids, repairs, and ear molds for Department of Social Development clients who have no other coverage. It covers up to $1,000 per hearing aid once every five years, at no cost to eligible clients.
intakeNote: Call Social Development at 1-833-733-7835; you need a valid Health Services card showing hearing aid eligibility.

name: Extra-Mural Program (home health care)
description: New Brunswick's home health care program, a Government of New Brunswick service that brings nurses, rehabilitation therapists, and other health professionals to your home. You, a family member, or any health care provider can send a request, and the Care Coordination Centre contacts the patient within two workdays.
intakeNote: Submit the online or printable request form at extramuralnb.ca, or call the Care Coordination Centre at 1-844-982-7367.

name: Home Support Services (Long Term Care Program)
description: A Government of New Brunswick program that helps seniors stay independent at home with personal care such as bathing and grooming, light housekeeping, meal preparation, and relief for family caregivers. A Social Development social worker visits to assess what services are needed.
intakeNote: Call the Department of Social Development at 1-833-733-7835 to ask for a long-term care assessment.

name: Homeowner Repair Program
description: A home repair program funded by the Government of Canada and the Government of New Brunswick and delivered by Housing NB. Low-income homeowners can get forgivable loans of up to $18,000 for urgent repairs, and seniors can get up to $7,000 for adaptations that make daily living at home easier.
intakeNote: Call Housing NB through Social Development at 1-833-733-7835 to apply.

name: Low-Income Seniors' Benefit
description: A Government of New Brunswick benefit that pays low-income seniors $629 a year (2026 amount). If you receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement or the federal Allowance, you can apply online, by mail, or at a Service New Brunswick centre by December 31 each year.
intakeNote: Apply online, by mail, or in person at Service New Brunswick between April 1 and December 31; call 1-833-796-0944 with questions.

name: Property Tax Deferral Program for Seniors
description: A Government of New Brunswick program that lets homeowners 65 and older put off paying the yearly increases in property tax on their main home. The deferred amount, plus interest, is only repaid when the home is sold or transferred.
intakeNote: Apply online, by mail, or at any Service New Brunswick centre by December 31 of the tax year; call 1-800-669-7070 with questions.

name: New Brunswick Seniors' Advocate (Office of the NB Advocate)
description: An independent office of New Brunswick's Legislative Assembly that advocates for people 65 and older. Its case specialists help seniors who feel treated unfairly by provincial programs, including nursing home and special care home costs, refused home repairs, and access to services, at no charge and in confidence.
intakeNote: Call 1-833-453-8653, email advocate-defenseur@gnb.ca, or send a message through the website; an Individual Case Specialist follows up.

name: Adult Protection (elder abuse and neglect)
description: A Government of New Brunswick service that investigates and responds when a senior is being abused or neglected, including self-neglect. Anyone can make a referral to the Department of Social Development, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
intakeNote: Call Social Development at 1-833-733-7835; referrals can be made day or night through the nearest regional office.

name: Nursing Home Services (Social Development)
description: The Government of New Brunswick's front door to nursing home care. The Department of Social Development approves all nursing home admissions after assessing a person's health and social needs, and families who cannot afford the full cost can apply for financial assistance.
intakeNote: Call the Department of Social Development at 1-833-733-7835 to start a long-term care assessment.

name: 65Plus Plan (NL Prescription Drug Program)
description: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador drug coverage for seniors who receive Old Age Security and the Guaranteed Income Supplement. Enrolment is automatic, and members pay only the dispensing fee, up to $6 per prescription, for covered drugs.
intakeNote: No application needed; a drug card is mailed automatically once Service Canada confirms you receive OAS and GIS. Call 1-888-859-3535 with questions.

name: 811 HealthLine (Newfoundland and Labrador)
description: The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador's free, confidential health line. Registered nurses answer 24 hours a day to help you decide what to do about symptoms, answer questions about topics like dementia care, and point you to services, with dietitian and mental health support also available.
intakeNote: Dial 811 any time; call 1-888-709-2929 if 811 does not work from your phone or internet phone service.

name: Home Support Program (NL Health Services)
description: The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador's home support program for seniors who need help with daily living. After a clinical assessment, families choose agency-managed care, self-managed care, or paid family caregiving, covering personal care, housekeeping, meals, and respite for caregivers.
intakeNote: Call the NL Health Services intake line for your zone: Eastern Urban 709-752-4835, Eastern Rural 709-786-5217, Central 1-833-210-8491, Western 1-866-566-3787, Labrador-Grenfell 1-833-284-4751; an income-based assessment decides how much the province pays.

name: Home Modification Program (NL Housing)
description: A Government of Newfoundland and Labrador program, delivered by NL Housing, that helps lower-income homeowners pay for accessibility changes like ramps, grab bars, and roll-in showers so seniors can stay home longer. Forgivable loans reach $7,500 now and double to $15,000 when the updated program reopens in Fall 2026.
intakeNote: New applications are paused until Fall 2026 except urgent cases identified by an occupational therapist; call the Avalon office at (709) 724-3196 or your regional NL Housing office to ask about timing.

name: Aging Well at Home Grant ($400)
description: A Government of Newfoundland and Labrador grant of $400 per household that repays low-income seniors for everyday services like snow clearing, lawn care, house cleaning, grocery and prescription delivery, foot care, dental work, and rides to appointments. Applications run on a yearly cycle with a March 31 deadline.
intakeNote: Apply by email to Aging.Well@nlhealthservices.ca or by mail to NL Health Services Central Zone in Gander; call 709-651-6273 for help. The 2026-27 application was not yet posted as of August 2026.

name: Caregiver Benefit ($400 a month, NL)
description: A Government of Newfoundland and Labrador benefit that pays $400 a month to an unpaid caregiver, such as a family member or friend, who regularly cares for a lower-income senior with high care needs. It recognizes the caregiver's role and helps keep the senior at home.
intakeNote: Download the application from the NL Health Services page and contact the Caregiver Benefit coordinator for your zone (Eastern Urban 709-752-4361); the care recipient needs a current NL Health Services assessment.

name: Office of the Seniors' Advocate NL
description: An independent office of Newfoundland and Labrador's House of Assembly that speaks up for seniors across the province. It reviews seniors' concerns about provincial programs, identifies systemic problems, and pushes government for change, and any senior or family member can contact it directly.
intakeNote: Call (709) 729-6603 or toll-free 1-833-729-6603, or email SeniorsAdvocate@SeniorsAdvocateNL.ca.

name: Newfoundland and Labrador Seniors' Benefit
description: A Government of Newfoundland and Labrador refundable tax credit that pays low-income seniors up to $1,882 a year. There is no application: file your income tax return each year and the money arrives in quarterly instalments with the federal GST Credit payments in January, April, July, and October.
intakeNote: File your annual income tax return; the CRA pays the benefit automatically. Call (709) 729-3166 with questions.

name: Special Assistance Program (medical equipment and supplies)
description: A Government of Newfoundland and Labrador program that provides basic medical equipment and supplies, such as wheelchairs, walkers, oxygen equipment, and orthotics, to people living at home who meet income rules.
intakeNote: Apply through the NL Health Services intake line for your zone (Eastern Urban 709-752-4835); a financial assessment checks eligibility.

name: Long-Term Care and Personal Care Home Placement
description: The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador's route into long-term care homes, which provide 24-hour nursing, and personal care homes, which provide supervision and support. One clinical assessment through NL Health Services starts the placement process, with an income-based subsidy for those who cannot pay the full cost.
intakeNote: Call your zone's NL Health Services intake line (Eastern Urban 709-752-4835) to request an assessment; the same call covers home support, personal care homes, and long-term care.

name: Adult Day Programs (Continuing Care)
description: Government of Nova Scotia day programs, arranged through Nova Scotia Health Continuing Care, where seniors spend the day in a supervised group with activities and company. They also give family caregivers regular daytime relief.
intakeNote: Call Continuing Care at 1-800-225-7225 to ask about adult day programs in your area.

name: 811 Nurse Line (Nova Scotia)
description: A free Government of Nova Scotia health line. Call 811 around the clock to talk to a registered nurse about symptoms, medications, or where to find care, with interpretation available in over 125 languages.
intakeNote: Dial 811 any time; call 1-866-770-7763 if you cannot reach 811.

name: Seniors' Pharmacare Program
description: The Government of Nova Scotia's drug plan for seniors without other coverage. Members pay an annual premium based on household income, plus a copayment with yearly maximums, and the province covers the rest; low-income seniors can have the premium reduced or waived.
intakeNote: An application package is mailed before your 65th birthday; apply online or on paper, and call 1-800-544-6191 for help. Renew by April 1 each year.

name: Continuing Care Home Care (Nova Scotia Health)
description: The Government of Nova Scotia's home care program, delivered through Nova Scotia Health. One call starts an assessment for nursing visits, personal care, essential housekeeping, and respite that gives family caregivers a break, either at home or in a licensed facility.
intakeNote: Call 1-800-225-7225 (8:30 am to 4:30 pm, seven days a week); a Care Coordinator arranges an in-home assessment.

name: Housing Repair and Accessibility Program
description: A Government of Nova Scotia program that helps low- and moderate-income homeowners, including seniors, pay for urgent health and safety repairs and accessibility adaptations so they can stay in their homes. It funds up to $18,000 as a grant and forgivable loan, with more available as a repayable loan for big jobs.
intakeNote: Call 1-844-424-5110 or mail the application to a regional housing office; emergency repairs are reviewed in 1 to 3 days.

name: Caregiver Benefit ($400 a month)
description: A Government of Nova Scotia benefit that pays $400 a month to a family member or friend who gives 20 or more hours a week of unpaid care to a low-income person with high care needs. It recognizes the caregiver's work and helps them keep going.
intakeNote: Call Continuing Care at 1-800-225-7225; both caregiver and care recipient are assessed.

name: Property Tax Rebate for Seniors
description: A Government of Nova Scotia rebate that returns half of the municipal property taxes a low-income senior paid last year, up to $800. If you receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement or the Allowance and your taxes are paid, you can apply until December 31 each year.
intakeNote: Mail the application with supporting documents or drop it off at Access Nova Scotia by December 31; rebates take 8 to 10 weeks.

name: Seniors Care Grant ($750)
description: A Government of Nova Scotia grant of $750 per household that repays low-income seniors for everyday help they buy, like snow removal, lawn care, house cleaning, grocery delivery, taxis, foot care, physiotherapy, small home repairs, and home heating. Applications open each fall and close March 31.
intakeNote: Apply online or by mail when the yearly window opens (recent rounds opened in September); call 1-800-670-4357 with questions. The 2026-27 round had not opened as of August 2026.

name: Adult Protection (report abuse or neglect)
description: The Government of Nova Scotia's service for adults who are being abused or neglected and cannot protect themselves. In Nova Scotia reporting is required by law, and anyone can call to report a concern about a senior; call 911 if a life is in danger.
intakeNote: Call 1-800-225-7225 to make a report; an Adult Protection worker investigates.

name: Personal Alert Assistance Program
description: A Government of Nova Scotia program that helps low-income seniors pay for a personal alert device or emergency response service, the kind you press for help after a fall. An assessment through Nova Scotia Health Continuing Care decides eligibility.
intakeNote: Call Continuing Care at 1-800-225-7225 to ask for a Personal Alert Assistance Program assessment.

name: Health Equipment Loan Program (hospital beds at home)
description: A Government of Nova Scotia program that loans fully electric hospital-style beds, pressure reduction mattresses, and bed rails to people who need them at home, free of charge.
intakeNote: Call Continuing Care at 1-800-225-7225; a Care Coordinator assesses whether a specialized bed is appropriate.

name: Seniors Community Wheelchair Loan Program
description: A Government of Nova Scotia program that provides manual and electric wheelchairs, new and recycled, to low-income seniors who need one for daily activities at home and in the community.
intakeNote: Call Continuing Care at 1-800-225-7225 to check eligibility and book an assessment.

name: Long-Term Care Placement (Continuing Care)
description: The Government of Nova Scotia's front door to nursing homes and residential care facilities. A Continuing Care Coordinator assesses your needs, helps choose the right option, and handles the application and wait list.
intakeNote: Call Continuing Care at 1-800-225-7225 to arrange an assessment.

name: Extended Health Benefits Seniors' Coverage
description: A Government of Nunavut health plan for residents 65 and older who are not covered through the federal Non-Insured Health Benefits program for Inuit and First Nations. It pays for formulary prescription drugs, up to $1,000 of dental care a year, vision care, hearing services, medical supplies and in-territory ambulance charges. Phone the Extended Health Benefits office to register.
intakeNote: Contact the EHB team to register and get claim forms: 867-645-8029, toll-free 1-800-661-0833, or ehb@gov.nu.ca.

name: Nunavut Home and Community Care
description: A Government of Nunavut program that sends helpers and nurses into the home for house cleaning, meals, personal care, wound care, respite for family caregivers and rehabilitation. Anyone enrolled in the Nunavut Health Care Plan can ask for it themselves through their community health centre, no doctor's referral needed.
intakeNote: Ask at your community health centre or local home care office, or phone the Territorial Home and Continuing Care Program at 867-975-5941; you can refer yourself or a family member.

name: Seniors Fuel Subsidy
description: A Government of Nunavut program that pays for up to 4,000 litres of heating fuel a year for seniors 60 and older who own and live in their home. Households with net income up to $75,000 get the full subsidy and those up to $100,000 get half. Your local Income Assistance Worker helps you apply each year.
intakeNote: Apply through your local Income Assistance Worker with proof of age, home ownership and last year's Notice of Assessment; regional offices: Qikiqtani 867-473-2600 or 1-800-567-1514, Kivalliq 867-645-5040 ext. 1604 or 1-800-953-8516, Kitikmeot 867-983-4032 or 1-800-661-0845.

name: NWT 811
description: A Government of the Northwest Territories phone service where registered nurses give health advice 24 hours a day, every day, in all NWT communities. The same line now includes mental wellness support and coaching to quit smoking or vaping. Dial 811, or 1-844-259-1793.
intakeNote: Dial 811 any time; alternate number 1-844-259-1793.

name: Extended Health Benefits for Seniors
description: A Government of the Northwest Territories health plan that gives seniors 60 and older no cost coverage for prescription drugs, dental care, vision care, medical supplies and equipment, and approved medical travel. It serves residents who are not covered by the federal Non-Insured Health Benefits program or Metis Health Benefits, and Alberta Blue Cross handles the claims.
intakeNote: Apply once with the Extended Health Benefits form through the Health Benefits Program; seniors do not re-apply each year; toll-free 1-800-661-0830 ext. 49462 or 867-777-7400.

name: NWT Home and Community Care
description: A Government of the Northwest Territories service that provides nursing, personal care, homemaking, respite, equipment loans and palliative support so people can stay in their own homes. Anyone with a valid NWT health care card can be referred for an assessment through their regional home care office or community health centre.
intakeNote: Phone your regional home care office: Yellowknife 867-920-3338, Beaufort-Delta 867-777-8150, Dehcho 867-695-7075, Fort Smith 867-872-6222, Hay River 867-874-7208, Sahtu 867-587-3650, Tlicho 867-392-6612; territorial office 867-767-9030.

name: Seniors Aging in Place (Housing NWT)
description: A Housing NWT program, part of the Government of the Northwest Territories, that gives homeowners 60 and older a forgivable loan of up to $15,000 for minor repairs, energy upgrades and small adaptations such as grab bars. Applications for 2026 are open April 1 to October 31 through your Housing NWT district office.
intakeNote: Phone your Housing NWT district office to start: North Slave (Yellowknife) 867-767-9332 ext. 85481, Beaufort Delta 867-678-8060, Nahendeh 867-695-7700, Sahtu 867-587-5100, South Slave 867-874-7600; a housing representative completes the application with you.

name: Seniors Home Repair (Housing NWT)
description: A Housing NWT program, part of the Government of the Northwest Territories, that provides a forgivable loan of up to $50,000 for major health and safety repairs to homes owned by seniors 60 and older. Applications for 2026 are open April 1 to October 31 through your Housing NWT district office.
intakeNote: Phone your Housing NWT district office to start: North Slave (Yellowknife) 867-767-9332 ext. 85481, Beaufort Delta 867-678-8060, Nahendeh 867-695-7700, Sahtu 867-587-5100, South Slave 867-874-7600; a 10 percent co-pay applies if household income is over $59,999.

name: Senior Home Heating Subsidy
description: A Government of the Northwest Territories subsidy that helps seniors 60 and older pay for heat in the home they own or a rented unit where heat is not included. Depending on community and income, eligible seniors receive $460 to $750 a month from September through April. Apply again each year.
intakeNote: Apply at your local ECE Service Centre with proof of age, household income and homeownership or rental; deadline March 15 for the current season; 867-767-9355 or toll-free 866-973-7252.

name: Income Assistance for Seniors and Persons with Disabilities
description: A Government of the Northwest Territories income program for residents 60 and older whose income does not cover their basic needs. It pays actual shelter and utility costs plus set amounts for food and other basics, based on family size and community. Client Navigators at ECE Service Centres help with the application.
intakeNote: Complete the application at your local ECE Service Centre with ID and financial information; main line 867-767-9355 or toll-free 866-973-7252.

name: Senior Citizens and Disabled Persons Property Tax Relief
description: A Government of the Northwest Territories program that removes all property tax for homeowners 65 and older in the General Taxation Area, which covers NWT communities outside the cities, towns and villages. Owners file a short sworn declaration form every year. Inside municipalities such as Yellowknife, the local government runs its own version of the relief.
intakeNote: Get the application form from maca.gov.nt.ca, a MACA office or your community government and file it each year; MACA regional offices: North Slave 867-392-6900, South Slave 867-872-6525, Deh Cho 867-695-7226, Inuvik 867-678-8045 ext. 21652, Sahtu 867-587-7100.

name: NWT Senior Citizen Supplementary Benefit
description: A Government of the Northwest Territories benefit that adds $196 a month to the income of low income seniors. Anyone receiving Old Age Security plus the Guaranteed Income Supplement or the Spouse's Allowance gets it automatically with their federal payment. Filing taxes each year keeps it coming.
intakeNote: Automatic once federal GIS or Spouse's Allowance is in place; questions to ECE income security at 867-767-9355 or toll-free 866-973-7252.

name: Assistive Devices Program: Hearing Aids and Visual Aids
description: An Ontario government program that helps pay for hearing aids and equipment for low vision. It covers 75 percent of the cost of hearing aids up to $500 per ear, and also funds approved visual aids and communication devices.
intakeNote: For hearing aids, get assessed by an ADP-registered audiologist or hearing instrument specialist and apply before you buy; the vendor submits the application.

name: Assistive Devices Program: Wheelchairs, Walkers and Mobility Aids
description: An Ontario government program that pays 75 percent of the approved price of mobility equipment such as wheelchairs, power scooters and wheeled walkers. People receiving Ontario Works or ODSP support pay nothing.
intakeNote: Get assessed by an occupational therapist or physiotherapist registered with ADP before buying; they help complete the application and the vendor submits it.

name: Ontario Caregiver Helpline
description: A free 24/7 helpline for anyone caring for a family member or friend, run by the Ontario Caregiver Organization and funded by the Government of Ontario. Callers get a listening ear plus help finding respite, support groups and community programs near them, in English and French with interpretation in 150 languages.
intakeNote: Call the helpline any time, 24/7; live chat is open weekdays 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.

name: Ontario Drug Benefit for Seniors 65+
description: The Ontario government drug plan that starts automatically the month after you turn 65. Once you have paid the first $100 of prescription costs in a program year, you pay no more than $6.11 for each covered prescription.
intakeNote: Enrollment is automatic at 65; the province mails a letter about 3 months before your 65th birthday. Call with questions or to check a drug is covered.

name: Seniors Co-Payment Program
description: An Ontario government top-up to the Ontario Drug Benefit for lower income seniors. It removes the $100 yearly deductible and drops the charge to no more than $2 per prescription.
intakeNote: Apply online at ontariodrugbenefit.ca or call to request a paper form; you can apply up to 3 months before turning 65 and renew each program year.

name: Trillium Drug Program
description: An Ontario government program for households that spend about 4 percent or more of their after-tax income on prescription drugs. After a deductible based on household income, you pay up to $2 per prescription, which helps spouses and family members who are under 65.
intakeNote: Apply online at forms.ontariodrugbenefit.ca or call for a paper form; enrollment renews automatically each year if you file your taxes on time.

name: Ontario Electricity Support Program
description: An Ontario Energy Board program that puts a monthly credit of $35 to $113 straight onto the electricity bill of lower income households. Apply online, by paper form or with free help from a local intake agency; if you are already behind on a bill, ask about the related Low-income Energy Assistance Program at the same time.
intakeNote: Apply online at ontarioelectricitysupport.ca, by paper form, or with free help from a local intake agency; the OESP contact centre answers questions at 1-855-831-8151.

name: Health Care Connect: Find a Family Doctor
description: An Ontario government service that puts you on the list for a family doctor, nurse practitioner or primary care team accepting new patients in your community. Register online or by phone and you are matched as spots open near you.
intakeNote: Register online through the Health Care Connect portal or call 811 (TTY: 711), available 24 hours a day; have your Ontario health card ready.

name: Health811 Nurse Advice Line
description: A free Ontario government line you can call day or night to talk to a registered nurse, get health advice and find services near you. Help is available in English, French and more than 300 other languages, by phone or online chat, and you can also ask to speak with a registered dietitian.
intakeNote: Call 811 (TTY: 711) any time, or chat online at health811.ontario.ca.

name: Ontario Health atHome Adult Day Programs
description: A public program coordinated by Ontario Health atHome, Ontario's public home and community care agency. Adult day programs offer recreational and social activities, meals, personal care, and basic health care in a small group community setting, giving older adults social connection and giving family caregivers a break.
intakeNote: Call 1-833-515-1234, available 7 days a week 365 days a year, and the call is automatically routed to the nearest local office; anyone, including the person themselves, a family member, or a doctor, can start a referral.

name: Ontario Health atHome
description: Ontario's public home and community care agency, a Government of Ontario Crown agency formerly known as Home and Community Care Support Services. Provides nursing, personal support, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and other in-home care coordinated by a care coordinator, covered through OHIP for people with a valid Ontario health card.
intakeNote: Call 1-833-515-1234, available 7 days a week 365 days a year, and the call is automatically routed to the nearest local office; anyone, including the person themselves, a family member, or a doctor, can start a referral.

name: Ontario Health atHome
description: Part of Ontario's public health system. Hospice palliative care nurse practitioners provide direct clinical care, pain and symptom management, and support in the home for people with a life-limiting illness, plus referrals to respite care, visiting volunteers, hospice day programs, hospice residences, and bereavement support.
intakeNote: Call 1-833-515-1234, available 7 days a week 365 days a year, and the call is automatically routed to the nearest local office; anyone, including the person themselves, a family member, or a doctor, can start a referral.

name: Long-Term Care Home Placement: Ontario Health atHome
description: Ontario Health atHome is the Ontario government agency every family goes through to apply for a long-term care home. A care coordinator assesses eligibility, helps you compare and choose homes anywhere in Ontario, and manages the application and wait list.
intakeNote: Call 1-833-515-1234 or start with the online request form; a care coordinator guides the rest of the process.

name: Long-Term Care Family Support and Action Line
description: The Ontario Ministry of Long-Term Care's line for concerns and complaints about long-term care homes. Call if a resident is being harmed or a problem is not being fixed; the ministry can send an inspector, and urgent complaints can get same-day action.
intakeNote: Call 1-866-434-0144, 8:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., 7 days a week; complaints can also be mailed or emailed to the ministry.

name: Office of the Public Guardian and Trustee
description: The Ontario government office that steps in as decision maker of last resort when an adult can no longer manage their money or make care decisions and there is no family member or attorney able to act. Families can also call its investigations unit if they believe a mentally incapable person is being harmed or financially abused (TTY 1-833-813-5696).
intakeNote: Call 1-800-891-0504, or email OPGT.Investigations@ontario.ca if you believe a mentally incapable adult is at risk of harm or financial abuse.

name: Ontario Seniors Dental Care Program
description: Free routine dental care for lower income seniors 65 and older, run by the Ontario government through public health units and partner clinics. It covers checkups, cleanings, fillings, x-rays, extractions and gum care, and pays part of the cost of dentures.
intakeNote: Apply online at seniors.accerta.ca, by mail, or with help from your local public health unit; coverage runs to July 31 each year and must be renewed.

name: Ontario Seniors Care at Home Tax Credit
description: A refundable Ontario government tax credit that gives seniors 70 and older back up to 25 percent of eligible medical and home care expenses, to a maximum of $1,500 a year. It is claimed on Form ON479 with the income tax return.
intakeNote: Claimed once a year on the senior's income tax return (ON-BEN or ON479 forms); GAINS needs no application for seniors already getting OAS and GIS.

name: Guaranteed Annual Income System (GAINS)
description: An Ontario government monthly payment that tops up the income of low-income seniors who already get Old Age Security and the Guaranteed Income Supplement. Payments of up to $92 a month for the 2026 benefit year arrive automatically; most seniors just need to file their tax return each spring to keep them coming.
intakeNote: Automatic for seniors already receiving OAS and GIS; otherwise file your income tax return by April 30 or send a GIS application to Service Canada.

name: Ontario Senior Homeowners' Property Tax Grant
description: An Ontario government grant of up to $500 a year that helps seniors with modest incomes pay the property tax on their home. It is claimed by filling in the ON-BEN form with the yearly income tax return.
intakeNote: Claimed once a year on the senior's income tax return (ON-BEN or ON479 forms); GAINS needs no application for seniors already getting OAS and GIS.

name: Ontario Trillium Benefit (energy and property tax help)
description: A monthly Ontario government benefit that combines the Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit, the Ontario Sales Tax Credit and the Northern Ontario Energy Credit into one payment. Seniors 65 and older qualify for a higher property tax credit, up to $1,488 a year.
intakeNote: File the yearly income tax return with the ON-BEN application form; payments then arrive automatically.

name: Patient Ombudsman
description: An independent office of the Ontario government that takes complaints about public hospitals, long-term care homes, home and community care, and surgical and diagnostic centres. It is free, and staff work to resolve concerns the organization itself could not fix.
intakeNote: Use the organization's own complaint process first; then complain online at patientombudsman.ca or call. Note the office closes at 12:30 p.m. on Thursdays.

name: Adult Day Programs (Health PEI)
description: Government of Prince Edward Island day programs where seniors enjoy games, crafts, exercise, and company in a safe, supervised setting, with a hot lunch and snacks included. Locations run across the Island, including a French program in Abram Village, and caregivers get a real break.
intakeNote: Contact the Home Care office in your area to be assessed (Charlottetown (902) 368-4790, Summerside (902) 888-8440, Montague (902) 838-0786, Souris (902) 687-7096, O'Leary (902) 859-8730); you arrange your own transportation.

name: 811 Telehealth (PEI)
description: The Government of Prince Edward Island's free health line. A registered nurse answers 24 hours a day to help you decide whether something needs urgent care, answer health questions, and point you to services on the Island.
intakeNote: Dial 811 any time (TTY 711); if 811 does not work from your phone, call 1-866-770-7724 from a PEI-registered line.

name: Seniors' Drug Program (PEI Pharmacare)
description: A Government of Prince Edward Island drug plan for everyone 65 and older with a PEI Health Card. There is no application; you are enrolled automatically at 65 and pay $8.25 plus a $7.69 pharmacy fee for each covered prescription, and the program pays the rest.
intakeNote: Enrolment is automatic at age 65; call PEI Pharmacare at 1-877-577-3737 with questions about coverage.

name: COACH Program (frail seniors at home)
description: A Government of Prince Edward Island program, run by Health PEI, that wraps a geriatric care team around frail seniors with complex health needs so they can stay at home longer and leave hospital sooner. A nurse practitioner coordinates care with your doctor and Home Care.
intakeNote: A referral is required from your doctor, nurse practitioner, geriatrician, or Home Care Coordinator; questions go to your local Home Care office (Charlottetown (902) 368-4790).

name: Home Care Program (Health PEI)
description: The Government of Prince Edward Island's public home care service, run by Health PEI. Nurses, home support workers, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, dietitians, and social workers come to your home, and the same team handles palliative care and long-term care assessments.
intakeNote: You, family, or your doctor can send the Home Care Referral form to your local office: Charlottetown (902) 368-4790, Summerside (902) 888-8440, Montague (902) 838-0786, Souris (902) 687-7096, O'Leary (902) 859-8730.

name: Seniors Home Repair and Seniors Safe @ Home Programs
description: Government of Prince Edward Island grants that help homeowners 60 and older fix and adapt their homes. One application covers up to $4,000 for essential repairs like a roof, windows, doors, or furnace, and up to $10,000 for accessibility changes so a senior can keep living at home safely.
intakeNote: Apply once online or on paper to the PEI Home Renovation Programs (902-368-4889 or toll-free 1-855-374-7366); seniors are automatically assessed for both seniors streams.

name: At Home Caregiver Benefit
description: A Government of Prince Edward Island benefit for seniors with high care needs who stay at home thanks to an unpaid family caregiver, friend, or neighbour. The person receiving care gets $250 to $1,500 a month depending on household income.
intakeNote: Call 1-800-371-8245 to start; Home Care completes an assessment, then the Department of Social Development and Seniors enrols you and sets the monthly amount.

name: Seniors Property Tax Deferral Program
description: A Government of Prince Edward Island program that lets lower-income seniors stop paying property tax on their home for as long as they live there, with no interest charged on the deferred amount. The taxes are only repaid when the home is sold or from the estate.
intakeNote: Send the application form to Taxation and Property Records with last year's Notice of Assessment for everyone in the home; call (902) 368-4070 with questions.

name: Seniors Independence Initiative
description: A Government of Prince Edward Island program that gives low-income seniors up to $1,800 a year to pay for practical help at home, such as light housekeeping, meal preparation, snow removal, grass cutting, transportation, internet, and a medical alert system.
intakeNote: Apply online, download the form, or pick one up at Access PEI; call 1-877-569-0546 for help completing it, then staff visit to assess your needs.

name: Seniors Navigators
description: A free Government of Prince Edward Island service where two provincial navigators help seniors, family members, and caregivers figure out which programs they qualify for, fill in applications, and reach the right office. They also hold drop-in outreach sessions in communities across the Island.
intakeNote: Call 1-866-770-0588 or email seniors@gov.pe.ca; you can also meet a navigator at a community outreach session or book an appointment.

name: Long-Term Care Placement (Health PEI)
description: The Government of Prince Edward Island's route into public and private nursing homes. A Health PEI Care Coordinator assesses whether nursing home care is needed, then you choose up to three homes for the wait list.
intakeNote: Start with your local Home Care office (Charlottetown (902) 368-4790); a Care Coordinator completes the assessment and manages the wait list.

name: Public Prescription Drug Insurance Plan (RAMQ)
description: The public drug plan run by RAMQ, the Government of Quebec's health insurance board, covering more than 8,000 prescription drugs. When you turn 65 you are registered automatically unless you choose to keep a private plan, and the annual premium is collected through your Quebec income tax return.
intakeNote: Registration at 65 is automatic; call RAMQ before turning 65 only if you are keeping private insurance.

name: Info-Sante 811
description: The Government of Quebec's free 24-hour health line. Dial 811 and choose option 1 to speak with a nurse about any non-urgent health problem, for yourself or a family member, every day of the year. It can spare a senior an unneeded trip to a clinic or emergency room.
intakeNote: Dial 811, option 1, any time, from anywhere in Quebec.

name: Free Eye Exams for Seniors 65+ (RAMQ)
description: Quebec Health Insurance Plan coverage, paid by the Government of Quebec through RAMQ, that gives adults 65 and over one free complete eye exam per year at the optometrist. Emergency eye exams are covered for everyone. Eyeglasses and contact lenses are not covered for adults.
intakeNote: Book with any Quebec optometrist and show a valid Health Insurance Card.

name: Hearing Devices Program (RAMQ)
description: A RAMQ program (Government of Quebec) that pays for hearing aids and assistive listening devices, including repair and replacement, for insured Quebecers with a qualifying hearing loss. Adults qualify with an average loss of at least 35 decibels in the better ear, confirmed by a hearing test.
intakeNote: See a Quebec audioprosthetist for a hearing aid, or a recognized specialized facility for assistive listening devices, with the required audiology documents.

name: Visual Devices Program (RAMQ)
description: A RAMQ program (Government of Quebec) that lends visual aids such as reading machines, braille devices and white canes to people with a permanent visual impairment, and pays set amounts toward getting and keeping a guide dog. The needs assessment is free with your health insurance card.
intakeNote: Apply through an accredited facility specializing in vision rehabilitation; the facility assesses your needs and lends the devices.

name: Financial Assistance Program for Domestic Help Services (RAMQ)
description: A Government of Quebec program managed by RAMQ that lowers the hourly rate you pay a recognized domestic help business for housekeeping, heavy cleaning, snow clearing at the entrance, laundry, meal preparation and accompanied errands. Everyone 18 and over with Quebec health insurance gets $4 off each hour, and up to $22.08 more per hour depending on age, income and family situation.
intakeNote: Contact a recognized domestic help social economy business; it gives you the application form and sends it to RAMQ for you.

name: Residential Adaptation Assistance Program (Programme d'adaptation de domicile)
description: A Societe d'habitation du Quebec program (Government of Quebec) that pays homeowners to adapt the home of a person with a significant, lasting disability, such as ramps, stair aids and accessible bathrooms, so they can stay home safely. Registrations reopen online on August 12, 2026 after a pause that began in April 2025. The program page is currently available in French only.
intakeNote: From August 12, 2026 at 8:30 a.m., register online through the Quebec.ca program page; call 1 800 463-4315, option 1 with questions.

name: Tax Credit for Home-Support Services for Seniors (70+)
description: A Revenu Quebec refundable tax credit that gives Quebecers 70 and over money back on home support expenses such as housekeeping, personal care and meal services, whatever their level of autonomy. It applies whether the senior owns a house, rents an apartment, lives with family or lives in a private seniors' residence, and it can be paid in advance through the year instead of at tax time.
intakeNote: Claim it in the Quebec income tax return (Schedule J), or register with Revenu Quebec for advance payments.

name: Grant for Seniors to Offset a Municipal Tax Increase
description: A Revenu Quebec grant that softens a sharp municipal tax increase caused by a jump in home value, for seniors 65 and over who have owned their home for at least 15 consecutive years. The home must be their principal residence and family income must be $64,200 or less.
intakeNote: Claim it on line 462 of the Quebec income tax return using form TP-1029.TM-V.

name: Quebec Pension Plan Retirement Pension (Retraite Quebec)
description: The Government of Quebec's public retirement pension, managed by Retraite Quebec, for anyone who contributed to the Quebec Pension Plan while working. You can start it as early as 60 at a reduced amount, take 100 percent at 65, or wait as late as 72 for a higher pension for life.
intakeNote: Apply online through My Account or with a paper form a few months before you want payments to start; you can cancel within six months of the first payment.

name: Senior Assistance Tax Credit
description: A Revenu Quebec refundable tax credit of up to $2,000 for a single senior or $4,000 for a couple where both spouses qualify, for lower-income Quebecers 70 and over. There is nothing to claim: Revenu Quebec calculates it automatically when the senior files a Quebec income tax return.
intakeNote: File a Quebec income tax return; the credit is calculated automatically.

name: Shelter Allowance Program
description: A Government of Quebec housing benefit, managed by Revenu Quebec for the Societe d'habitation du Quebec, that pays up to $170 a month to low-income renters, boarders and homeowners who spend 30 percent or more of their income on housing. People 50 and over living alone or as a couple can qualify, subject to income limits.
intakeNote: Apply online in My Account for individuals or with the paper application; both spouses must have filed Quebec tax returns.

name: Mistreatment Helpline (Ligne Aide Maltraitance)
description: A confidential provincial helpline for older adults facing abuse, neglect or financial exploitation, and for worried family members. It is funded by the Government of Quebec's Secretariat for Seniors and staffed by counsellors who specialize in mistreatment, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. every day. Formerly known as the Elder Mistreatment Helpline (Ligne Aide Abus Aines).
intakeNote: Call 1-888-489-2287 any day between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m.; anonymous and bilingual.

name: Caregiver Support Helpline (Info-aidant)
description: A free professional listening and referral line for family caregivers, run by L'Appui pour les proches aidants, a nonprofit funded by the Government of Quebec. Trained counsellors help caregivers find respite, local services and financial aid in their region, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., by phone or online chat.
intakeNote: Call 1 855 852-7784 or use the website chat, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.

name: Info-Social 811
description: The Government of Quebec's free 24-hour psychosocial help line. Dial 811 and choose option 2 to speak confidentially with a professional about worry, grief, loneliness, family conflict or a mental health concern, for yourself or someone you care for.
intakeNote: Dial 811, option 2, any time, from anywhere in Quebec.

name: Devices That Compensate for a Physical Deficiency (RAMQ)
description: A RAMQ program (Government of Quebec) that pays for wheelchairs, walking aids, orthoses, prostheses and posture aids for insured Quebecers with a physical impairment. Devices come through authorized public rehabilitation facilities and approved laboratories. Scooters and walkers fall under separate government assistive device programs.
intakeNote: Go to an authorized public rehabilitation facility (or an authorized laboratory for orthoses and prostheses); a medical prescription is sometimes required.

name: Independent Living Tax Credit for Seniors
description: A Revenu Quebec refundable tax credit for people 70 and over that pays back part of the cost of buying, leasing and installing equipment that helps them keep living at home, and of stays in a functional rehabilitation transition unit after a hospital stay. It is a Government of Quebec benefit claimed through the income tax return.
intakeNote: Keep receipts and claim the credit at line 462 of the Quebec income tax return.

name: Financial Contribution Program for Accommodated Adults (RAMQ)
description: RAMQ, the Government of Quebec's health insurance board, sets the monthly amount you pay for room and board in a public long-term care home (CHSLD) or other public facility. Care itself is free; the room costs up to $2,242.20 a month for a private room, and families who cannot afford the set amount can apply for a reduction based on ability to pay.
intakeNote: Placement is arranged through your CISSS or CIUSSS assessment; once admitted, RAMQ mails the notice of decision and you can file an Application for Exemption or Re-Evaluation to lower the amount.

name: Regina Public Library Home Library Service
description: A Regina Public Library service, part of the city's public library system, for people who cannot get to a branch for three months or more because of age, illness, or disability. Library staff pick books and other items to match your tastes and have them delivered right to your home. Residents of Regina care facilities and seniors' care homes can use it too.
intakeNote: Call Accessibility Services at 306.777.6048 or email accessibilityservices@reginalibrary.ca to enroll.

name: Peel Adult Day Services
description: A Region of Peel program that gives frail seniors and adults living with dementia or chronic illness a welcoming place to spend the day, with activities, meals, and personal care at all five Peel long term care centres. It also gives family caregivers a regular daytime break. A free virtual program is available for those who cannot attend in person.
intakeNote: Apply through Ontario Health atHome: call 310-2222 (or 1-877-336-9090 for Mississauga Halton, 1-888-733-1177 for Central West) and a Peel Adult Day Services coordinator will follow up.

name: Thrive Program (dementia care at Peel Manor)
description: A Region of Peel program, part of the Ontario government's Community Access to Long-Term Care pilot, that wraps dementia-focused primary care, geriatric specialists, social work, and adult day programming around seniors living at home in the community. Care is based at the Seniors Health and Wellness Village at Peel Manor in Brampton, with in-person and virtual visits.
intakeNote: Call 905-791-6905 ext. 1691 or email seniorsservices@peelregion.ca to ask about joining; the program confirms eligibility with the family.

name: Peel overnight respite stays for caregivers
description: A Region of Peel service that gives family caregivers a planned break: the person they care for stays overnight in a safe, staffed setting at the Seniors Health and Wellness Village at Peel Manor in Brampton (stays of about one to two weeks) or the Davis Centre in Caledon. Daily activities and personal care are included.
intakeNote: Call the Integrated Care Coordinator at 905-791-6905 ext. 7663 or email seniorsservices@peelregion.ca; booking 6 to 8 weeks ahead is recommended, and short-notice stays are sometimes possible.

name: Peel property tax rebate for low-income seniors
description: A Region of Peel program that gives low-income senior homeowners a yearly rebate on their property taxes, covering the city, Region, and school board portions. Council sets the rebate amount each year and it does not have to be repaid.
intakeNote: Apply through your city tax office before December 31 of the tax year: Mississauga 905-615-4311 or Brampton 905-874-2200. You must reapply every year.

name: TransHelp (Region of Peel accessible transit)
description: TransHelp is the Region of Peel's shared-ride, door-to-door public transit for people whose disability keeps them from using regular buses some or all of the time. It serves Mississauga, Brampton, and Caledon, and there is no fee to apply. Seniors 65 and older also ride regular MiWay buses free with a senior PRESTO card, and Brampton Transit offers discounted senior fares.
intakeNote: Apply online through the Peel resident portal, or by mail, fax, or email; call 905-791-1015 and press 2 for application questions. Decisions come within 14 days.

name: Retirement Homes Regulatory Authority
description: The regulator that licenses retirement homes across Ontario under the province's Retirement Homes Act. Before choosing a home, families can search its free public database for licence status and inspection history, and anyone can call to complain or report harm to a resident.
intakeNote: Search the database online or call 1-855-ASK-RHRA (1-855-275-7472); reports of harm can be made by anyone, not just residents.

name: STAC Paratransit Quebec City (Transport adapte de la Capitale)
description: Door-to-door adapted transit for Quebec City residents whose disability keeps them off the regular bus, run by the RTC transit authority as the STAC (Service de transport adapte de la Capitale). Admission is by a form your health professional helps complete, then trips are booked by phone or online. Seniors who can use the regular bus pay reduced fares with the RTC's OPUS Aine photo card instead.
intakeNote: Download the admission form from rtcquebec.ca or call 418 687-2641, option 2 to have it mailed; a health professional completes part of it, and the admission committee answers within 45 days. Once admitted, book trips by phone or online.

name: HealthLine 811
description: A free Government of Saskatchewan health advice line answered 24 hours a day by registered nurses, registered psychiatric nurses, and registered social workers. Call 811 for help deciding what to do about symptoms, or for mental health and addictions support, with translation available in over 100 languages.
intakeNote: Just dial 811 any time, day or night; if 811 does not connect, call 1-877-800-0002, and deaf or hard of hearing callers can use SaskTel Relay at 1-800-855-0511.

name: Seniors' Drug Plan
description: A Government of Saskatchewan program that caps what seniors 65 and older pay for eligible prescription drugs at $25 per prescription. Drugs must be on the Saskatchewan Formulary or approved under Exception Drug Status, and eligibility is based on the net income on your tax return.
intakeNote: Apply once by mail, fax, or email using Form A, which lets the Canada Revenue Agency confirm your income so coverage renews automatically every year; you can apply up to two months before you turn 65. Call 1-800-667-7581 or 306-787-3317 with questions.

name: Seniors Education Property Tax Deferral Program
description: A Government of Saskatchewan program, run by Saskatchewan Housing Corporation, that lets senior homeowners put off paying the education portion of their property taxes through a repayable loan. It helps seniors on fixed incomes stay in their homes without falling behind on tax bills.
intakeNote: Complete the application form and send it to Saskatchewan Housing Corporation in Regina by email or mail, or apply in person at 1920 Broad Street; call 1-800-667-7567 or 306-787-4177 with questions.

name: Seniors Income Plan (SIP)
description: A Government of Saskatchewan program that adds a monthly payment of up to $360 to the income of seniors who have little or no income besides Old Age Security and the Guaranteed Income Supplement. There is no application form. If you qualify, the benefit starts automatically once you file your income tax return and receive OAS and GIS, and clients also get extra provincial health benefits.
intakeNote: No application needed; eligibility is set automatically from your income tax return and your OAS/GIS from Service Canada, and is reassessed each July. Call 306-787-2681 or 1-800-667-7161 with questions.

name: Saskatchewan Aids to Independent Living (SAIL)
description: A Government of Saskatchewan program that provides equipment and supplies to people with physical disabilities and certain chronic conditions so they can live independently at home. It includes wheelchair and special needs equipment loans plus programs for prosthetics, orthotics, home oxygen, CPAP machines, and compression garments.
intakeNote: You need a referral from an authorized health care professional such as a doctor or therapist; call SAIL toll-free at 1-888-787-8996 or 306-787-7121 with questions.

name: Personal Care Home Benefit
description: A Government of Saskatchewan benefit that gives seniors monthly financial help with the cost of living in a licensed personal care home. It tops up a resident's monthly income toward a $3,500 threshold, based on income and marital status.
intakeNote: Download the application form and send it with your GIS entitlement letter or recent tax return to the Ministry of Social Services Client Service Centre in Regina by mail, email, or fax; call 1-855-544-7242 with questions.

name: Saskatoon Public Library Accessibility Services (home delivery)
description: A Saskatoon Public Library service, part of the city's public library system, that gets books and other materials to Saskatoon residents who cannot come to a branch because of age, disability, or extended illness. Items can be delivered to your home or sent to your nearest branch for easy pickup. The same team runs a talking book service for people with print disabilities and lends DAISY audiobook players to try at home.
