intakeNote: Call Accessibility Services at 306.975.7565 or email access@saskatoonlibrary.ca and complete the short loan application form.

name: Allowance and Allowance for the Survivor (ages 60 to 64)
description: Tax-free monthly Government of Canada payments for people aged 60 to 64 with low income. The Allowance is for the spouse or common-law partner of a senior who gets the Guaranteed Income Supplement, and the Allowance for the Survivor is for someone whose spouse or partner has died. Apply 6 to 11 months before you turn 60, or right away if you are already in this age range.
intakeNote: You must apply; call Service Canada or apply through My Service Canada Account.

name: Canada Pension Plan (CPP) retirement pension
description: A monthly taxable Government of Canada pension that replaces part of your income in retirement and is paid for life to people who contributed to the CPP while working. You can start it as early as 60 or wait until 70 for a larger amount. If you keep working while collecting before age 70, extra contributions earn a post-retirement benefit that raises your pension each year.
intakeNote: You must apply; apply online through My Service Canada Account or call. If you worked in another country, international social security agreements may help you qualify.

name: CPP disability benefits
description: A monthly taxable Government of Canada benefit for people over 18 and under 65 who cannot work because of a severe and prolonged disability and who contributed to the CPP. People already collecting a CPP retirement pension who become disabled before 65 may qualify for the post-retirement disability benefit instead. At 65 it converts automatically to the regular CPP retirement pension.
intakeNote: You must apply, and a health care professional completes the medical part of the application; apply through My Service Canada Account or by paper form.

name: CPP survivor's pension and death benefit
description: Government of Canada payments to the family of a CPP contributor who has died. The survivor's pension is a monthly payment to the legal spouse or common-law partner, and the death benefit is a one-time payment of up to $5,000 to the estate or the person who paid the funeral costs. Apply as soon as possible after the death, because the survivor's pension can only be back-paid for 12 months.
intakeNote: Apply online through My Service Canada Account or by mail as soon as possible after the death.

name: EI caregiving benefits (family caregiver and compassionate care)
description: Employment Insurance benefits from the Government of Canada that replace part of your pay while you are away from work caring for someone. The family caregiver benefit covers up to 15 weeks for a critically ill or injured adult, and compassionate care benefits cover up to 26 weeks for a person who needs end-of-life care. You do not have to live with or be related to the person, and eligible caregivers can share the weeks.
intakeNote: Apply online at canada.ca as soon as you stop work, with a medical certificate for the person you care for; call 1-800-206-7218 for help with a claim.

name: Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS)
description: A tax-free monthly top-up from the Government of Canada for seniors 65 and older who receive the OAS pension and have low income. It is worth checking even if you are not sure you qualify, and you must file your income tax return every year to keep the payments coming.
intakeNote: Many seniors are enrolled automatically and told by letter; if no letter has arrived a month after your 64th birthday, call Service Canada or apply through My Service Canada Account.

name: Old Age Security (OAS) pension
description: A monthly Government of Canada pension for people 65 and older, based on how long you have lived in Canada after age 18, whether or not you ever worked. Many seniors are enrolled automatically and get a letter from Service Canada; if no letter has arrived a month after your 64th birthday, you may need to apply. Years spent in countries that have a social security agreement with Canada can help you qualify.
intakeNote: Call Service Canada or apply online through My Service Canada Account; many seniors are enrolled in OAS and GIS automatically and get a letter in the mail around their 64th birthday.

name: Ontario death certificates
description: ServiceOntario, the Ontario government's service counter, is the only official source for Ontario death certificates, which families need to cancel a health card, claim insurance and settle the estate. Order online for $15, by mail or in person; regular online orders arrive in about 15 business days.
intakeNote: Order online at services.ontario.ca, by mail, or in person at the Toronto and Ottawa centres; call 1-800-267-8097 with questions.

name: Ontario Photo Card
description: Government photo ID from the Ontario government for people who do not drive, handy when a senior gives up their licence but still needs official ID for banking, travel bookings and appointments. Apply in person at a ServiceOntario centre; the card is valid for 5 years.
intakeNote: Apply in person at a ServiceOntario centre with identity documents; call 1-800-267-8097 with questions.

name: Accessible Parking Permit
description: A free Ontario government permit that lets a person with a walking limitation or other qualifying condition park in accessible spaces in any vehicle they are travelling in, as driver or passenger. A doctor, nurse, physiotherapist or other listed practitioner certifies the form, then you apply online, by mail or at a ServiceOntario centre.
intakeNote: Call ServiceOntario or visit a ServiceOntario centre; many services can also be done online at ontario.ca.

name: Soldiers' Aid Commission of Ontario
description: An Ontario government agency that gives veterans and their families up to $3,000 in a 12 month period for essentials such as home repairs, housing costs, health items, specialized equipment and personal needs. Many older veterans qualify; applications go through the Royal Canadian Legion or Veterans Affairs Canada.
intakeNote: Apply through the Royal Canadian Legion at 1-888-207-0939 (sac@on.legion.ca) or Veterans Affairs Canada at 1-866-522-2122, with quotes for the expense and recent bank statements.

name: GoBus Accessible Transit (Metrobus)
description: GoBus is the accessible, door-to-door transit service run by Metrobus under the St. John's Transportation Commission, a municipal public agency, for people whose disabilities keep them off regular buses. It serves St. John's and neighbouring Mount Pearl, with service seven days a week into the late evening. Apply with a form partly completed by a healthcare professional, take a short transit assessment paid for by Metrobus, then book rides by phone.
intakeNote: Submit the GoBus application form, with one section completed by a healthcare professional, to Accessible Transit Services at 25 Messenger Drive; a Metrobus-funded transit assessment follows, then registered riders book at (709) 368-8887.

name: STL Transport adapte (Laval paratransit)
description: Door-to-door adapted transit for Laval residents whose disability significantly limits their mobility, an STL (Societe de transport de Laval) service. STL reviews applications and manages rider files, and approved riders book trips through the reservation centre. Seniors 65 and over who can ride the regular bus travel free anywhere in Laval with the STL's Horizon 65+ photo OPUS card.
intakeNote: Apply through STL at 450-688-6520 or transportadapte@stl.laval.qc.ca; once admitted, reserve trips at 450-973-3111.

name: STL Seniors Residence Shuttle Lines
description: Weekly bus shuttles that pick seniors up at participating Laval residences and bring them to nearby shopping centres for the morning, an STL (Societe de transport de Laval) service. Four lines each run one day a week in Chomedey, Vimont, Sainte-Rose and Laval-des-Rapides, and the ride is free for seniors 65 and over with the Horizon 65+ card.
intakeNote: No registration needed; board at your residence's scheduled stop, or call 450 688-6520 for schedules.

name: STM Paratransit (Transport adapte)
description: Door-to-door shared rides across the island of Montreal for people whose disability keeps them off the regular bus and metro, an STM (Societe de transport de Montreal) service. After a one-time application, riders book trips by phone or online and pay regular transit fares. Seniors 65 and over who live in the Montreal agglomeration also ride the regular STM network free with a 65+ photo OPUS card.
intakeNote: Apply with the Transport adapte admission form on stm.info, or call 514 280-8211 (option 4, customer service, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.) to get started; approved riders book trips by phone, online, or in the Mon transport adapte portal.

name: STO Transport adapte (Gatineau paratransit)
description: Door-to-door adapted transit for Gatineau residents whose disability keeps them off the regular bus, an STO (Societe de transport de l'Outaouais) service run through a contracted carrier. Admission uses a form your health professional helps complete, then trips are booked by phone or online, seven days a week. Seniors 65 and over who can use the regular bus pay reduced STO senior fares instead.
intakeNote: Call 819 773-2222, option 3, or download the eligibility form from sto.ca; a health professional completes part 2, you send it to admission.ta@sto.ca or by mail, and STO answers within 45 days. Admitted riders book trips at the same number, option 1.

name: Temmy Latner Centre for Palliative Care
description: Physicians from the Temmy Latner Centre visit patients with serious, life-limiting illness in their own homes across Central Toronto and North York. It is a hospital-affiliated program of Sinai Health, part of the public hospital system, and a physician referral is required to start care.
intakeNote: A physician faxes a referral form to the Temmy Latner Centre; there is no self-referral route listed on Sinai Health's own site.

name: Toronto Public Library Home Library Service
description: A free City of Toronto library service that delivers up to 20 books, audiobooks, magazines, CDs and DVDs to your door every month. It is for Toronto residents who cannot get to a library for three months or longer because of age, illness, mobility or disability, and staff pick items to match your reading interests.
intakeNote: Call 416-395-5557 or email hls@tpl.ca; library staff confirm eligibility and set up the monthly delivery day.

name: Toronto Seniors Helpline
description: One phone number that connects Toronto seniors and their caregivers to home care referrals, community supports, counselling and crisis help. It is publicly funded through Ontario Health and answered by WoodGreen Community Services with partner agencies, 365 days a year, with interpretation in over 100 languages.
intakeNote: Call 416-217-2077 (or 1-877-621-2077 long distance); calls are answered 365 days a year and interpretation is available in over 100 languages.

name: Ajax 55+ Programs and Seniors Centre Without Walls
description: The Town of Ajax runs recreation, fitness and social programs for adults 55 and over, including Seniors Centre Without Walls, a free program of activities you can join from home by phone or Zoom. There are also social lunches, a free indoor walking program from November to March, dances and wellness fairs.
intakeNote: Call 365-282-6025 or email 55plus@ajax.ca; register for programs through the town's recreation guide at ajax.ca/55plus.

name: Ajax Public Library Visiting Library Service
description: Ajax Public Library, the Town of Ajax's library system, delivers books, large print, magazines, audiobooks and DAISY talking books each month to residents who cannot visit a branch because of illness, injury or disability. Long-term, winter seasonal and temporary service options are available.
intakeNote: Complete the Visiting Library Service application and email it to libraryinfo@ajaxlibrary.ca or drop it at any branch; call 905-683-4000 ext. 8850 with questions.

name: Ajax Snow Removal Program for Qualified Residents
description: A Town of Ajax winter service for seniors 65 and over and residents with disabilities who have no one at home able to shovel. Crews clear snow after storms of more than 5 cm, including driveways and the pathway to the front door, starting about 24 hours after the snow stops. Runs November to April.
intakeNote: Fill out the Snow Removal Program application at ajax.ca/snow or call Operations and Environmental Services at 905-683-2951 (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.) for details and pricing.

name: Oakville Seniors Services and Older Adult Centres
description: The Town of Oakville runs six older adult centres, including Sir John Colborne, Trafalgar Park and Sixteen Mile, with social, recreational, health and wellness programs for residents 50 and over. An annual membership of about $60 covers drop-in programs, costs less at 80, and is free from age 90.
intakeNote: Buy a membership and register online, in person at any centre, or by calling 905-815-2000.

name: Oakville Public Library Delivery by Mail
description: Oakville Public Library, the Town of Oakville's library system, mails library materials free of charge to residents who cannot come into a branch. Qualifying customers can receive up to two packages of two items each month, with return postage covered.
intakeNote: Email oplbymail@oakville.ca or call your local branch (Central Branch 905-815-2042) to find out if you qualify and get set up.

name: Oakville Driveway Windrow Snow Clearing Program
description: A paid Town of Oakville service that clears part of the windrow, the snow pile the plow leaves across the driveway, within about 36 hours of a snowfall from December 1 to March 31. Seniors 65 and over and residents with disabilities get priority registration in early October before spots open to everyone.
intakeNote: Register in October through ServiceOakville at 905-845-6601 or oakville.ca; priority registration for 65+ and residents with disabilities runs October 1 to 15.

name: Oakville Senior's Property Tax Rebate
description: A Town of Oakville rebate of $500 in 2026 for senior homeowners with low incomes. Seniors 65 and over who receive the monthly Guaranteed Income Supplement can apply each fall and the rebate is applied to their property taxes.
intakeNote: Submit the Senior's Property Tax Rebate application or renewal with proof of GIS by the fall deadline printed on the form; questions to tax@oakville.ca or ServiceOakville at 905-845-6601.

name: Oakville Transit care-A-van
description: The Town of Oakville's door-to-door accessible transit service for people whose disability prevents them from using the regular bus. Rides are free as of May 1, 2025, and run seven days a week using accessible vehicles and partnered taxis.
intakeNote: Apply with the specialized transit form (a health care professional signs Part B), submitted by email to mobility@oakville.ca, fax or in person; once approved, book trips at 905-337-9222 or through the On Demand app.

name: Whitby 55+ Programs and Services
description: The Town of Whitby runs recreation, fitness, clubs and social programs for adults 55 and over, including the Mingles Café where older adults can drop in for refreshments and company on weekday mornings. Staff can also point families to town services like the snow clearing program and tax clinic.
intakeNote: Call 905-668-1424 or email 55plus@whitby.ca; program registration is online through the town's recreation system.

name: Whitby Public Library Visiting Library Service
description: Whitby Public Library, the Town of Whitby's library system, delivers books and other materials to residents who cannot get to a branch because of illness, disability or other circumstances. Staff choose items to match your tastes and volunteers deliver on a regular schedule.
intakeNote: Apply with the Patron Application Form on the library website, or call the Central Library at 905-668-6531.

name: Whitby Windrow and Sidewalk Snow Clearing Program
description: A free Town of Whitby service for seniors 65 and over and residents with disabilities who have no one at home able to shovel. Town crews clear the ridge of snow the plow leaves at the end of the driveway and any public sidewalk beside the property, usually within about 36 hours after the snow stops.
intakeNote: Register online each fall; applications for the coming winter open September 14, 2026 and close November 1, 2026.

name: Whitby Low Income Seniors Property Tax Rebate
description: A Town of Whitby rebate that takes several hundred dollars off the yearly property tax bill for senior homeowners with low incomes. You qualify if you are 65 or older, receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement, and own and live in your Whitby home. A matching program exists for low-income homeowners with disabilities on ODSP.
intakeNote: Send the application form with a copy of your current GIS letter to tax@whitby.ca or the Tax Department at 575 Rossland Rd E by December 31; apply again each year.

name: Whitby 55+ Free Income Tax Clinic
description: Each spring the Town of Whitby's 55+ Services runs a free drop-off clinic where trained volunteers prepare basic income tax returns for older adults with modest incomes. Filing every year protects benefits like GIS, the Ontario Trillium Benefit and tax credits.
intakeNote: Runs March 1 to April 30 each year as a drop-off clinic; call 905-668-1424 or email 55plus@whitby.ca to take part.

name: HandyDART (TransLink, Metro Vancouver)
description: A TransLink service that gives door-to-door, shared rides across Metro Vancouver, including the City of Vancouver, for people who cannot use regular buses or SkyTrain without help. Drivers assist riders to and from the vehicle. Fares are the same as regular transit, with a lower concession fare for riders 65 and older.
intakeNote: Apply first with the HandyDART application form (approval takes about 10 days); call 604.953.3680 for help applying. Once registered, book trips at 604.575.6600 or toll-free 1.844.475.6600.

name: Wheel-Trans (TTC accessible door-to-door transit)
description: The City of Toronto's para-transit service, run by the TTC, giving door-to-door rides to people whose disability makes regular transit difficult. Riders apply once, then book trips online, in the app, or by phone, including same-day bookings.
intakeNote: Apply online at portal.ttc.ca or call Customer Service 416-393-4111; once registered, book trips at mywheel-trans.ttc.ca or call Reservations 416-393-4222.

name: Funeral and Burial Assistance (Last Post Fund)
description: A Veterans Affairs Canada program, delivered by the nonprofit Last Post Fund, that helps pay funeral, burial and grave marker costs so eligible veterans receive a dignified funeral. Families apply through the Last Post Fund within one year of the veteran's death.
intakeNote: Call the Last Post Fund at 1-800-465-7113 to apply; applications must be submitted within one year of the veteran's death.

name: Veterans Independence Program (VIP)
description: A Veterans Affairs Canada program that pays for housekeeping, grounds maintenance, meal preparation, personal care and other supports so veterans can keep living in their own homes. Some survivors and primary caregivers of deceased veterans can also receive housekeeping and grounds maintenance funding.
intakeNote: Call Veterans Affairs Canada at 1-866-522-2122, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm local time, or apply online through My VAC Account.

name: VAC Assistance Service
description: A free Veterans Affairs Canada helpline that connects veterans, former RCMP members, their families and caregivers with a mental health professional at any hour, every day of the year. Callers can receive up to 20 hours of confidential counselling and do not need an existing VAC file.
intakeNote: Call 1-800-268-7708 any time, day or night (TDD/TTY 1-800-567-5803); no referral or VAC file needed.

name: Veterans Affairs Canada Long-term Care Support
description: A Government of Canada program that helps pay nursing home costs for veterans who need 24-hour personal and nursing care. The veteran pays a capped monthly amount toward room and meals, currently $1,236.90, and Veterans Affairs Canada helps with eligible care costs beyond that.
intakeNote: The veteran must first be admitted to a long-term care home, then the family applies through My VAC Account online or mails application package VAC1503APe; call 1-866-522-2122 for help.

name: Gatineau Library Home Delivery
description: Free delivery of library books and other documents to your home for library subscribers aged 70 and over or with reduced mobility, a Ville de Gatineau municipal library service (livraison de documents a domicile). Call the library to sign up and materials come to your door at no charge.
intakeNote: Call the Bibliotheque municipale de Gatineau at 819-595-7460 or use the contact form on gatineau.ca to register for home delivery.

name: Laval Libraries Home Delivery (Pret a domicile)
description: Free delivery of library books and other items to your home, five times a year, for people with reduced mobility or loss of autonomy and for family caregivers, a Ville de Laval public library service (Bibliotheques de Laval, Pret a domicile). Register through your neighbourhood library in person or by phone, or by emailing bibliomobile@laval.ca.
intakeNote: Call 311 (450 978-8000 from outside Laval) or use the Mon dossier portal on laval.ca; the 65+ subsidy is applied for online or by mail, and the library home delivery is arranged through your neighbourhood library.

name: Laval Subsidy for People 65 and Over
description: A yearly cash subsidy from the Ville de Laval for households with a resident aged 65 or over (Subvention pour favoriser le soutien des personnes agees de 65 ans et plus): $150 per dwelling, or $300 when the applicant receives the federal Guaranteed Income Supplement. Owners, tenants and occupants can all apply online through Mon dossier or by mail, and it is separate from Quebec's provincial municipal tax grant.
intakeNote: Call 311 (450 978-8000 from outside Laval) or use the Mon dossier portal on laval.ca; the 65+ subsidy is applied for online or by mail, and the library home delivery is arranged through your neighbourhood library.

name: Acces-Loisirs Montreal (Free Recreation for Low Income)
description: Free spots in sports, culture and leisure activities for Montrealers with a modest income, seniors included, a Ville de Montreal program run with local community groups (Acces-Loisirs). You sign up in person during registration periods held each season in 14 participating boroughs.
intakeNote: Call 311 (514 872-0311 from outside Montreal) or email acces-loisirs@montreal.ca, then register in person at your borough's posted registration dates.

name: Bibliomobile Home Library Delivery (Quebec City)
description: Free home delivery of books, films and other library items for subscribers 75 and over or with reduced mobility, a Ville de Quebec public library service (Bibliotheque de Quebec, called Bibliomobile). A security-checked volunteer from your neighbourhood borrows the items, brings them to your home and returns them, and it works from every library in the network.
intakeNote: Fill in the Bibliomobile form on bibliothequedequebec.qc.ca, or call 418 641-6789 or your neighbourhood library to register; a security-checked volunteer from your sector then brings library items to your door.

name: VON Seniors Lunch Bunch (Dining Programs)
description: Seniors Lunch Bunch brings older adults together for a hot meal and social activities like music, games, or a guest speaker, three days a week at three Mississauga locations. VON Canada is a national registered charity, and this is a public community care service, not a privately vetted company.
intakeNote: Families can call VON's national toll-free line, but most of the specific programs below require a referral through Ontario Health atHome (formerly Home and Community Care Support Services) rather than a direct booking, so the fastest path is usually the regional number listed for each program.

name: VON Home Support
description: VON Home Support sends personal support workers into people's homes for bathing, dressing, light housekeeping, mobility help, and medication supervision in Mississauga, South Etobicoke (Toronto), and Brampton. VON Canada is a national registered charity, and this program is part of Ontario's public home and community care system, reached through a referral rather than a direct booking.
intakeNote: Families can call VON's national toll-free line, but most of the specific programs below require a referral through Ontario Health atHome (formerly Home and Community Care Support Services) rather than a direct booking, so the fastest path is usually the regional number listed for each program.

name: VON Meals on Wheels
description: VON Meals on Wheels delivers hot or frozen meals to people who cannot cook for themselves, with a volunteer safety check at every hot delivery. Available in Mississauga (except Malton), Oakville, and South Etobicoke in Toronto. VON Canada is a national registered charity, and this is a public community care service.
intakeNote: Families can call VON's national toll-free line, but most of the specific programs below require a referral through Ontario Health atHome (formerly Home and Community Care Support Services) rather than a direct booking, so the fastest path is usually the regional number listed for each program.

name: VPL Accessible Services and Home Delivery
description: A Vancouver Public Library service, run by the city's own library staff, that delivers books and other library materials to the door of Vancouver residents who cannot get to a branch because of illness, injury or disability. Deliveries come every 4 weeks, and a special audiobook collection is available for people who cannot read regular print.
intakeNote: Fill out the Accessible Services registration form and email it to accessible@vpl.ca or bring it to any branch; call 604.331.4100 with questions.

name: Winnipeg Transit Plus
description: Winnipeg Transit Plus is a City of Winnipeg service that gives pre-booked, door-to-door shared rides to people who cannot regularly use regular buses because of a disability. Drivers help riders between a ground floor doorway and the vehicle, and trips can be booked by phone, app, or online. Seniors 65 and older who can still ride regular buses pay a reduced seniors fare on Winnipeg Transit.
intakeNote: Apply online or with the printable form, then Winnipeg Transit may invite you to a functional assessment; call 204-986-5722 daily 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. with questions or to book trips.

name: WoodGreen Friendly Visiting
description: WoodGreen's Friendly Visiting program sends trained volunteers for in person social visits and wellness checks to seniors 55 and older and adults with disabilities who are experiencing social isolation. This is a free program run by a registered charity, available year round in Toronto.
intakeNote: A family calls WoodGreen's Central Intake line, Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., to register for Meals on Wheels, the Transportation Program, or Friendly Visiting.

name: WoodGreen Meals on Wheels
description: WoodGreen delivers hot and frozen meals to seniors 55 and older and adults with disabilities who cannot prepare their own food, with a wellness check at every drop off. This is a program of a registered charity, and meals are fee based, from about $2.50 to $8.00 each depending on the type.
intakeNote: A family calls WoodGreen's Central Intake line, Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., to register for Meals on Wheels, the Transportation Program, or Friendly Visiting.

name: WoodGreen Transportation Program
description: WoodGreen's Transportation Program gives seniors 55 and older and adults with disabilities accessible rides to medical appointments, day programs, and group shopping within east and central Toronto. This is a program of a registered charity, with fees based on distance, starting at $7.20 for a short ride.
intakeNote: A family calls WoodGreen's Central Intake line, Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., to register for Meals on Wheels, the Transportation Program, or Friendly Visiting.

name: York Region Adult Day Programs
description: York Region runs adult day programs at the Maple Health Centre in Vaughan and in Keswick, where seniors enjoy activities, social time, and a nutritious daily lunch, with dedicated programs for people living with aphasia or an acquired brain injury. Fees apply and subsidies are available for qualified participants.
intakeNote: Referral goes through Ontario Health atHome at 1-888-470-2222; for program information call 1-877-464-9675 ext. 76079.

name: York Region Homemakers Services
description: York Region helps cover the cost of an in-home homemaker for residents with a temporary or permanent illness or disability who meet financial need requirements. Homemakers help with laundry, meals and light housekeeping so people can keep living at home.
intakeNote: Call Access York at 1-877-464-9675 to apply; eligibility includes both the health need and a financial assessment.

name: York Region property tax deferral for low-income seniors
description: York Region lets low income senior homeowners defer property tax increases interest free, a program running since 1998. It is for homeowners 65 and older who receive the federal Guaranteed Income Supplement, and the deferred taxes are repaid only when the home is sold or transferred outside the family.
intakeNote: Apply through your local tax office: Markham 905-477-7000, Vaughan 905-832-2281, Richmond Hill 905-771-8800, Newmarket 905-953-5300, Aurora 905-727-1375.

name: York Region Client Intervention and Support Services
description: A free, non-crisis York Region service for seniors 60 and older offering in-home assessments, counselling, referrals and advocacy on hard subjects like elder abuse, money worries, bereavement, family relationships and future planning. It is open to seniors across York Region, not just housing residents.
intakeNote: Call 1-877-464-9675 (TTY 711) to be connected with the seniors support team.

name: YRT Mobility On-Request (accessible transit)
description: York Region Transit's door-to-door, shared ride, accessible public transit service for people whose disability prevents them from using regular buses some or all of the time. Riders apply once, then book trips by phone, live chat, online, or with the On-Request app.
intakeNote: Apply with the Mobility On-Request application package on yrt.ca (a health professional completes part), or call 1-888-762-2950 (TTY 711) for help; eligibility is decided case by case.

name: Seniors and Elders Community Day Program
description: A Government of Yukon day program at Whistle Bend Place in Whitehorse for seniors and Elders with mild to moderate memory loss, such as dementia. It offers group activities, meals, help with personal care and a break for family caregivers, Monday to Friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
intakeNote: Phone the admissions and assessment coordinator at 867-456-6806 or toll-free 1-800-661-0408 extension 6806; the coordinator completes the referral and arranges a tour.

name: Yukon HealthLine 811
description: Yukon HealthLine is a 24-hour phone service provided through the Government of Yukon. Registered nurses answer health questions any time of day, and an after-hours pharmacist is available from 5 pm to 9 am. Dial 811 from anywhere in the Yukon.
intakeNote: Dial 811 any time; from a satellite phone call 1-604-215-4700.

name: Yukon Pharmacare and Extended Health Care Benefits for Seniors
description: A Government of Yukon benefit that helps seniors 65 and older pay for prescription drugs, dental care, eye care and medical supplies and equipment. Eligible seniors are enrolled automatically and receive the sign-up form in the mail. Spouses aged 60 to 64 who are married to an eligible senior can also qualify.
intakeNote: Enrolment is automatic; the application arrives by mail. Questions: 867-667-5403 or toll-free 1-800-661-0408.

name: Yukon Home Care Program
description: A Government of Yukon program that brings nursing, home support, therapy, palliative, rehabilitation and respite care into homes across the territory. You can refer yourself or a family member by phone, and home care staff visit to assess what is needed.
intakeNote: Phone to arrange an assessment: Whitehorse 867-667-5774 (toll-free 1-877-667-5774), Dawson City 867-993-5029, Haines Junction 867-634-7510, Watson Lake 867-536-5256; staff complete the referral form with you over the phone.

name: Home Repair Program (Yukon Housing Corporation)
description: A Government of Yukon program run by the Yukon Housing Corporation that funds repairs for low and moderate income homeowners. It includes an Accessibility Grant of up to $30,000 to retrofit a home for someone with mobility challenges, an Emergency Repair Grant of up to $10,000 and a repair loan of up to $70,000. Applications are open all year while funding lasts.
intakeNote: Submit the application with documents in person at 410 Jarvis Street in Whitehorse or by email to ykhouse@yukon.ca; questions 867-667-5759 or toll-free 1-800-661-0408; wait for written approval before starting work.

name: Pioneer Utility Grant
description: A Government of Yukon grant that helps seniors 65 and older with the cost of heating their home, whether they own or rent. The amount depends on income, marital status and address, up to $1,382.58 inside Whitehorse and $1,466.50 outside for 2026. Apply each year between July 1 and December 31.
intakeNote: Apply online through the Pioneer Utility Grant portal, in person at the Income Support Unit in Whitehorse, or by mail; toll-free 1-800-661-0408 extension 4.

name: Seniors' Property Tax Deferment
description: A Government of Yukon program that lets homeowners 65 and older postpone paying property taxes on the home they live in. It applies outside municipalities, in areas where the Government of Yukon collects property tax. You can defer all or part of each year's taxes, up to 75 percent of the home's assessed value.
intakeNote: Contact the Property Assessment and Taxation office or a Territorial Agent for an application; 867-667-5268 or toll-free in Yukon 1-800-661-0408 ext. 5268; apply any time after January 1, before July 2 to avoid penalties.

name: Yukon Seniors Income Supplement
description: A Government of Yukon top-up of up to $323.26 a month for low income seniors who receive Old Age Security and the Guaranteed Income Supplement. There is no application form; payments start automatically once the federal government shares your GIS information with Yukon. Filing your taxes every year keeps the supplement coming.
intakeNote: Automatic for Yukon seniors receiving GIS; for questions call 867-667-5674 or toll-free 1-800-661-0408 extension 5674.

name: Adult Protection Services
description: A Government of Yukon service that responds when a senior or other adult is being abused, neglected or unable to care for themselves. Social workers plan next steps with the adult to reduce harm and improve safety, and callers can stay anonymous. Phone 911 if someone is in immediate danger.
intakeNote: Phone 867-456-3946 or toll-free 1-800-661-0408 extension 3946, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm; all reports are handled by Adult Protection Services in Whitehorse.
